# Rock Frost Business Suite — Operator Handoff

## 2026-09-05: Fixed two live production crashes found while re-checking a user report - a Server→Client boundary break in `buttonVariants()` and in the support inbox's `renderRow` prop

- **Scope**: while re-verifying the Fleet driver dropdown report (entry below), the user pasted two Vercel request logs (`GET /app/platform/support`, `GET /app/accounting`) that both showed `Status: 200`. That status is misleading for this class of bug: a React Server Components response can commit its `200` header, then fail while streaming the payload - `get_runtime_errors` showed a real, currently-live error at the exact timestamp of each pasted request. Both were genuine, currently-live production crashes, unrelated to the dropdown report and unrelated to each other.
- **Bug 1 - `buttonVariants()` called from the server (confirmed, fixed)**: the same-day Button pending-state fix (entry below) added `"use client"` to `src/components/ui/button.tsx`. Every export of a `"use client"` module becomes a client reference under React Server Components, including a plain, non-component function - so the seven Server Component files that imported `buttonVariants` from `button.tsx` to build a className string for a plain `<a>`/`<Link>` styled as a button (not rendering `<Button>` itself) crashed with "Attempted to call buttonVariants() from the server but buttonVariants is on the client" on every render. This broke `/app/accounting` directly, plus `/app/accounting/invoices`, `/app/accounting/cashbook`, `/app/accounting/bills`, and `/app/accounting/reconciliations/[id]`, and - transitively, through the two shared `report-export-links.tsx`/`report-download-links.tsx` components - every module's Reports page (19 routes: School, Projects, Procurement, POS, Pharmacy, Payroll, Inventory, Installment, HR, Hotel, Hostel, Hospital, Fleet, CRM, and five Accounting sub-pages). Live for roughly 90 minutes between the button fix's deploy and this one. Fixed by moving the `cva()` definition into a new `src/components/ui/button-variants.ts` with no `"use client"` directive; `button.tsx` now imports it instead of defining it locally, and all seven Server Component call sites now import `buttonVariants` from the new module instead of from `button.tsx`.
- **Bug 2 - `renderRow` function prop crossing the Server→Client boundary (confirmed, fixed, pre-existing since 2026-08-28)**: both `/app/platform/support` and `/app/support/inbox` are Server Components that passed an inline arrow function as the `renderRow` prop to `SupportConversationList`, a `"use client"` component. A plain function (anything not a `"use server"` action) cannot cross that boundary as a prop - React throws "Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components" - so both inbox pages have been unable to render since the shared conversation-list component was introduced, over a week before this session. Fixed by changing `SupportConversationList`'s prop from `renderRow: (conversation) => ReactNode` to `rows: { conversation, node }[]`: each page now pre-renders every row's JSX itself (already-rendered React elements are safe to pass as children across the boundary) and passes the array in, instead of a function the client component would have had to call itself.
- **Important files**: `src/components/ui/button-variants.ts` (new), `src/components/ui/button.tsx`, `src/app/app/accounting/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/accounting/invoices/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/accounting/cashbook/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/accounting/bills/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/accounting/reconciliations/[reconciliationId]/page.tsx`, `src/components/reports/report-export-links.tsx`, `src/components/reports/report-download-links.tsx`, `src/components/support/support-conversation-list.tsx`, `src/app/app/platform/support/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/(overview)/support/inbox/page.tsx`, `test/button-variants-server-boundary.test.ts` (new), `test/support-conversation-list.test.ts`, `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`, `docs/SUPPORT_MESSAGING.md`.
- **Schema and environment**: no migration, no environment-variable change.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean. `npm run lint` - zero errors, only the same two pre-existing, already-disclosed `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings. `npm run test` - full suite, 167 files/1,287 tests, all passing, including the 10 new tests asserting every Server Component importer pulls `buttonVariants` from the non-client module and 2 new tests asserting neither inbox page passes a `renderRow` function. `npm run build` - clean, all routes (including the previously-broken accounting and report pages) compiled. Not yet re-verified against the real dev server or production for either bug at the time of this entry - see the next dated entry for deployment and post-deploy verification.

## 2026-09-05: Fixed Fleet driver-report data leakage across vehicle reassignment, a Teacher seeing org-wide revenue, and silent submit buttons

- **Scope**: four issues reported in one batch by the user. Two confirmed real bugs in Fleet maintenance scoping, one confirmed permission leak on the main dashboard, and one confirmed app-wide UX gap (no loading feedback on submit buttons). A fifth reported symptom (a newly invited driver seeing every vehicle in the "Report an issue" dropdown) was investigated thoroughly and does not reproduce against current `main` - documented below rather than "fixed" with no real defect found.
- **Fleet maintenance data leak (confirmed, fixed)**: `FleetVehicle.assignedDriverId` is reassignable, but every place surfacing a driver's maintenance history scoped by vehicle, never by who actually reported the request. A driver taking over a reassigned vehicle inherited the predecessor's fault descriptions, identity, and uploaded photos. Fixed in three places: `getFleetDriverWorkspace()` now filters `maintenanceRequests` to `requestedById: userId`; `listFleetMaintenanceRequests()` gained an optional `requestedById` scope, applied on the shared `/app/fleet/maintenance` page only for a driver-only viewer (managers/owners still see every requester within their scope, as intended); `getFleetMaintenanceAttachment()` now checks the request's actual `requestedById` instead of "currently drives this vehicle." See `docs/HARDENING_PLAN.md`'s 2026-09-05 Fleet section for full detail, including why the "sees all vehicles in the dropdown" report doesn't reproduce in code.
- **Dashboard revenue leak (confirmed, fixed)**: `/app/dashboard`'s Revenue insights card summed every module's posted revenue org-wide, gated only on whether Accounting was active - never on the viewer's role. A Teacher, or any other non-admin operational role without a Fleet-style dedicated workspace to redirect to instead, landed on this same unscoped card. Added `isOrganizationOwnerRole()` alongside the existing `isOrganizationAdminRole()` (which had zero call sites before this fix, despite existing for exactly this purpose); the dashboard now never fetches `getRevenueInsights()` at all unless the viewer is Owner or Admin.
- **Silent submit buttons (confirmed, fixed)**: clicking a submitting button showed no loading feedback anywhere in 106 of the 113 files with a plain `<Button type="submit">` - a real risk of double-submission from repeated clicks. Fixed centrally in the shared `Button` component (`src/components/ui/button.tsx`): a plain submit button with no caller-managed `disabled` now auto-detects the enclosing form's pending state via `useFormStatus()`, disables itself, and shows a spinner with a fallback `aria-label`, with zero changes needed at any of the 228 files that import it. `EntityDialog` (~80+ callers) dropped its own now-redundant hand-rolled version of the same thing. See `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`'s Component conventions section.
- **Important files**: `src/modules/fleet/service.ts`, `src/app/app/fleet/maintenance/page.tsx`, `src/lib/auth/permissions.ts`, `src/app/app/(overview)/dashboard/page.tsx`, `src/components/ui/button.tsx`, `src/components/forms/entity-dialog.tsx`, `test/fleet-maintenance-attachments.test.ts`, `test/integration/tenant-isolation/fleet-driver-sales.test.ts`, `test/dashboard-and-accounting-trends.test.ts`, `test/button-pending-state.test.ts` (new), `docs/HARDENING_PLAN.md`, `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`.
- **Schema and environment**: no migration, no environment-variable change.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean. `npm run lint` - zero errors, only the same two pre-existing, already-disclosed `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings. `npm run test` - full suite, 166 files/1,275 tests, all passing, including new unit tests for all three Fleet scoping fixes, the dashboard gate, and Button's pending behavior. `npm run build` - clean. **Manually verified the Button fix against the real dev server**: a throwaway probe route (created, exercised with Playwright, then deleted before finishing) confirmed a plain, previously-unhandled submit button now auto-disables, sets `aria-busy`, and shows a spinner the instant a slow Server Action starts; the pre-existing custom-pending login button (which manages its own `disabled`) was confirmed completely unaffected. The new Fleet reassignment-scenario integration test could not be run locally (no `TEST_DATABASE_URL` in this sandbox) and needs CI's real-Postgres `integration` job to confirm it passes for real.
- **Remaining/open item**: the "newly invited driver sees every vehicle in the dropdown" report has no corresponding code defect on current `main` after a thorough audit (permission grants, every dropdown's data source, `hasPermission()`'s fail-closed behavior, custom-role shadowing). If it recurs, get the specific organization and driver account so the affected role's actual stored permissions can be inspected directly rather than assumed from the generic flow.
- **Deployed to production**: this batch was folded into the still-open PR #23 below (same session, same branch) rather than opened separately, since GitHub only carries one open PR per branch. PR #23's title/description were updated to cover both scopes before merging. On the updated head, `security` and `validate` were green; `integration` failed only on the same pre-existing `test/integration/settlement-activation-lifecycle.test.ts` (`PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY` unset) gap disclosed on every PR today - and critically, **the new real-Postgres Fleet reassignment regression test passed for real** (confirmed by name in the job log; the suite's total pass count increased by exactly the one new test added). Squash-merged as `1cc97a8`. Vercel deployment `dpl_CSgqW4jcbinMcuzYY3gBxvtU9sN8` reached `READY` and is aliased to `app.rockfrostgroup.com`/`www.rockfrostgroup.com`/`admin.rockfrostgroup.com`/`rockfrostgroup.com`. `get_runtime_errors` (last hour) showed zero errors attributable to this deployment - the only entries were the pre-fix subscription-cancel crash (see below), both timestamped before this deploy and attributed to the prior deployment, and an unrelated, pre-existing NextAuth `NO_SECRET` warning dating back to 2026-08-09. Nothing from the Fleet, dashboard, or Button/EntityDialog changes appeared as a new error.

## 2026-09-05: Fixed a live production 500 on platform subscription cancellation, and abandoned module checkouts sticking at "pending payment"

- **Scope**: two related subscription/billing bugs, one reported by the user as a live production 500 (caught via a real Vercel runtime-error report pasted mid-session) and one reported directly ("when a client is making payment for a module and he cancels, the system should reset. It shouldn't go to pending payment").
- **Production crash, confirmed live**: `POST /app/platform/subscriptions` was throwing `Error: Paystack automatic renewal is not fully registered. Cancel it from Paystack before cancelling local access.` as an unhandled request error (`get_runtime_errors` showed the exact stack trace). Root cause: `cancelSubscriptionAction` (`src/app/app/platform/subscriptions/actions.ts`) was the only action in that file with no `try`/`catch` around its service call, unlike its three sibling actions in the same file, which all already redirect with a friendly `?error=...` on failure. `cancelSubscription()`'s own business rule (refuse to cancel local access for an auto-renewing Paystack subscription until it's fully registered with Paystack) is correct and intentional; it just had nowhere safe to land. Gave that error its own class, `PaystackRenewalNotRegisteredError`, so the action can catch and redirect with a specific, actionable message instead of crashing. Also added the `create`/`activate`/`cancel` entries the page's `ERROR_MESSAGES` map was missing (those two other actions' failure redirects were rendering nothing at all before this).
- **Abandoned checkout reset**: a self-service module purchase creates a `Subscription` row at `PENDING_PAYMENT` before redirecting to the gateway. Cancelling at Paystack/Flutterwave, or a declined card, left that row stuck at `PENDING_PAYMENT` forever, since neither gateway callback page ever reset it - and `createSelfServiceSubscription()`/its cart/bundle variants block a new purchase attempt for the same product while any non-`CANCELLED`/`EXPIRED` row exists, so the customer's next attempt failed with a confusing "already has an active or pending subscription" error despite never being charged. Added `resetAbandonedCheckout()` (`src/platform/subscriptions/service.ts`), called from both callback pages whenever the gateway's verification is a definitive non-success (Flutterwave's explicit `status=cancelled` param, or `verification.success === false` from either provider) - never on a thrown verification error, which is left alone so the webhook can still catch up a payment that might still complete. It only ever deletes a subscription that is exactly `PENDING_PAYMENT` with no `activatedById` and no `paidAt`, so a `PAST_DUE` renewal-retry or anything ever `ACTIVE` is never touched even if that retry is itself cancelled.
- **Important files**: `src/platform/subscriptions/service.ts`, `src/app/app/platform/subscriptions/actions.ts`, `src/app/app/platform/subscriptions/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/(overview)/organization/billing/callback/paystack/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/(overview)/organization/billing/callback/flutterwave/page.tsx`, `test/subscription-gateway-payment.test.ts`, `docs/BILLING_AND_SUBSCRIPTIONS.md`.
- **Schema and environment**: no migration, no environment-variable change.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean. `npm run lint` - zero errors, only the same two pre-existing, already-disclosed `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings. `npm run test` - full suite, 165 files/1,264 tests, all passing, including 7 new unit tests (`resetAbandonedCheckout`'s five cases covering the delete-vs-never-touch boundary, and `cancelSubscription`'s two cases covering the new error class and the normal-path Paystack disable + local cancel). `npm run build` - clean. Not separately re-verified against a real Paystack/Flutterwave sandbox (this environment cannot receive an inbound webhook or complete a real hosted checkout), consistent with this doc's existing "Honestly unverified" note on the checkout round-trip; the production crash itself, however, was confirmed against a real `get_runtime_errors` report before and will be reconfirmed clear after deploy.
- **Deployed to production**: merged as part of PR #23 (squash commit `1cc97a8`) together with the Fleet/dashboard/button batch above - see that entry's "Deployed to production" line for the full CI and deployment record (`dpl_CSgqW4jcbinMcuzYY3gBxvtU9sN8`, `READY`). Specifically for this fix: `get_runtime_errors` confirmed the exact `Paystack automatic renewal is not fully registered` crash that started this fix has not recurred since deploy - both prior occurrences are timestamped before this release and attributed to the previous deployment. No online-gateway checkout-cancellation flow could be exercised for real in this environment (no way to reach Paystack/Flutterwave's hosted checkout from here); that half of the fix rests on the unit-test coverage of `resetAbandonedCheckout()`'s exact delete/never-touch boundary, not a live sandbox transaction.

## 2026-09-05: Centralized rate limiting for API routes and Server Actions

- **Scope**: user asked earlier whether rate limits were added to the endpoints; the answer was "selectively" (per-feature cooldowns for login lockout, invitation resend, the contact form, customer feedback, and AI support replies, but no generic throttle across the app's ~28 API routes or ~99 Server Action files). The user then asked to add it. Added one centralized, database-backed rate limiter enforced from `src/proxy.ts`, the single choke point every API route and every Server Action already passes through, instead of instrumenting each file individually.
- **Why this is possible without new infrastructure**: Next.js 16 changed `proxy.ts` (renamed from `middleware.ts`) to default to the Node.js runtime rather than Edge (confirmed in the installed `node_modules/next/dist/docs` for this exact version, 16.2.12), so Prisma can query Postgres directly inside it. No Redis/Upstash dependency was introduced.
- **Design**: every request to `/api/*` (any method) and every non-GET/HEAD request to any other path (a Server Action invocation is itself a POST to the page route that calls it) is checked. Identity is `user:<id>` from the NextAuth JWT when signed in (no DB hit to resolve it), else `ip:<address>`. Two fixed windows, tracked in a new `RateLimitBucket` table via one atomic `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`: `auth` (5 min / 30 requests) for `/api/auth/*` and non-GET requests to `/login`, `/forgot-password`, `/reset-password`, `/invite`; `general` (60 sec / 300 requests) for everything else in scope, sized against this app's actual measured polling load (support chat and notification-badge polling top out around 50-70 requests/min across a few open tabs for one user). Exempt entirely: the Paystack/Flutterwave webhook routes (signature-verified, provider-shared IP pools, and the rate-limit check must never read their body ahead of the downstream raw-body signature check), the cron routes (already `CRON_SECRET`-gated, fired only a few times a day), `/api/health` (an external uptime probe, where a false 429 reads as a false downtime alert), and the offline-sync routes (device-signature authenticated, legitimately bursty). The check fails open (logs and allows the request through) on any internal error, a deliberate, documented exception to this codebase's general fail-closed bias, matching the existing "never throws" precedent already stated for audit logging. On a block: JSON `429` for `/api/*`, and a `429` with a `text/plain` body (no charset) for Server Actions, matched to the exact shape the installed Next.js client needs to surface the message on the thrown error; either way `src/app/app/error.tsx` catches it as a normal error boundary.
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma` (new `RateLimitBucket` model), `prisma/migrations/20260905013939_add_rate_limit_bucket/`, `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` (new), `src/proxy.ts` (rewritten; `config.matcher` now also covers `/api/*`, which it previously excluded), `test/rate-limit.test.ts` (new), `test/proxy-host-routing.test.ts` (updated for the now-async `proxy()`), `docs/HARDENING_PLAN.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/OPERATIONS_AND_MONITORING.md`.
- **Schema and environment**: one new additive migration (`RateLimitBucket`, no changes to existing tables). No environment-variable change.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean. `npm run lint` - zero errors, only the same two pre-existing, already-disclosed `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings. `npm run test` - full suite, 165 files/1,257 tests, all passing, including the 9 new rate-limit unit tests (under-cap allow, user-id vs. IP keying, block shapes for both Server Action and API route branches, exact-cap boundary, tier isolation, and fail-open on both a DB throw and a token-lookup throw). `npm run build` - clean, Proxy (Middleware) compiled. **Could not run locally**: this sandbox has no `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, so the new migration itself was only verified with a schema-only `prisma migrate diff` run (produces the exact SQL committed, touches no live database) and needs CI's real-Postgres `integration` job to confirm it applies cleanly before merging. The exact `Content-Type: text/plain` (no charset) behavior this depends on for a good Server Action error message is worth a quick post-deploy sanity check in production, since a mismatch there would still be caught by the same error boundary with a generic message, not a crash.
- **Remaining risk**: the `general` tier's 300/min cap is sized from measured polling patterns, not load-tested against real concurrent multi-tenant traffic; watch `[rate-limit]` warnings and any user-reported false 429s after deploy and adjust the cap in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` if needed. `RateLimitBucket` rows are never pruned; at these caps and window sizes row count stays bounded by active-identity count, not request volume, but a periodic cleanup (e.g. delete rows with `windowStart` older than a day) would be a reasonable follow-up if the table grows unexpectedly.
- **Deployed to production**: pushed to `claude/latest-deployed-updates-bk4j2j`, opened as PR #21 against `main` (no merge conflict). On PR #21's CI, `security` and `validate` were green; `integration` failed, but the "Migrate the disposable test database" step succeeded first, confirming the new `RateLimitBucket` migration applies cleanly against real Postgres - the test step's only failures were the same pre-existing `test/integration/settlement-activation-lifecycle.test.ts` (`Paystack is not configured (PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY unset)`) already disclosed and confirmed unrelated on every earlier PR today (#15 through #20). Posted the standing-down comment, re-ran once (identical result: 55/56 files, 281/283 tests), then squash-merged as `de9da80fc51a49a3cb22a1f02d14bce3fa7969e9`. Vercel deployment `dpl_6fZiuWh588gd1MJMCzssDvHLEb4c` reached `READY` and is aliased to `app.rockfrostgroup.com`/`www.rockfrostgroup.com`/`admin.rockfrostgroup.com`/`rockfrostgroup.com`. `get_runtime_errors` (last hour) reported no runtime errors at all - zero, including nothing attributable to the new `proxy.ts` rate-limiting logic or `/api/health`. The exact `Content-Type: text/plain` Server Action behavior and a real sustained-burst 429 were not separately re-verified against live production traffic beyond this; treat a future report of an unexpected 429 or a missing rate-limit error message as the first place to look.

## 2026-09-04: Fixed the shared Team page's missing AppShell (sidebar disappeared, page stretched full-width)

- **Scope**: user reported that visiting `/app/pos/staff` made the sidebar disappear and the page stretch. Initial diagnosis (before a concurrent session's work landed) treated `/app/pos/staff` as a dead link with no matching page and prototyped a 404-handling fix; that fix was discarded once a concurrent session's "Shared team management across operational modules" release (`174604c`/`4c41025`, the entry immediately below this one) landed on `main` mid-investigation and made `/app/pos/staff` a real page (`src/app/app/[moduleKey]/staff/page.tsx`, a shared Team directory used by eleven modules). Re-diagnosed against that real page instead of the stale premise.
- **Root cause**: `src/app/app/[moduleKey]/staff/page.tsx` and its `actions.ts` shipped with no `layout.tsx` at `src/app/app/[moduleKey]/`. Every other route in the app gets its sidebar from a module-specific `layout.tsx` wrapping the page in `AppShell` (see "How module isolation is enforced structurally" in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`); this new dynamic segment had none, so it rendered directly under the bare authenticated `src/app/app/layout.tsx` (auth/tenant/providers only) - no sidebar, and the page's plain `<div className="space-y-6">` content had no width constraint either, since that normally comes from `AppShell`'s own `<main>` wrapper. This affected all eleven modules using the shared Team page (CRM, Inventory, Procurement, Accounting, Payroll, Analytics, POS, Projects, Hotel, Pharmacy, Hospital), not only POS - the user just happened to report it against POS first.
- **Fix**: added `src/app/app/[moduleKey]/layout.tsx`. It resolves `getModuleTeamConfig(moduleKey)` (404s for an invalid key, same as the page already did), gates on `canAccessModule(tenant, config.key)` the same way every real module layout does, then computes that specific module's `sectionLabel`/`navigation` and renders `AppShell` with it. For Inventory, Procurement, and Payroll (the three modules whose real layouts compute navigation dynamically rather than importing a static array) it calls the exact same helper functions their own `layout.tsx` files call (`getInventoryProcurementNavigation`/`getInventoryProcurementSectionLabel`, `getPeopleAndPayrollNavigation`), so the Team page's sidebar can never drift from that module's real pages.
- **Verified locally** against the real dev server (Next.js 16.2.12): confirmed via server logs that `/app/pos/staff`, `/app/crm/staff`, `/app/inventory/staff`, `/app/procurement/staff`, `/app/payroll/staff`, `/app/accounting/staff`, `/app/hotel/staff`, and even `/app/randomthing/staff` (an invalid module key) all resolve to `routePath: "/app/[moduleKey]/staff"` and behave correctly (redirect to login unauthenticated, no crash for the invalid key), and that every real module page (`/app/pos`, `/app/pos/registers`, `/app/crm`, `/app/inventory`, `/app/procurement`, `/app/payroll`, `/app/accounting`, `/app/school/staff`) still resolves to its own distinct route, confirming the new dynamic layout doesn't shadow anything. Could not visually confirm the rendered sidebar against a real authenticated tenant (no seeded session in this sandbox).
- **Test coverage gap closed**: the existing `test/module-team-management.test.ts` only ever checked file contents as strings (permission calls, navigation links) and never checked that the page renders inside an `AppShell` at all - which is exactly how this shipped broken. Added a test asserting `src/app/app/[moduleKey]/layout.tsx` exists, contains `<AppShell`, `requireCurrentTenant`, and the module-access gate, and has a chrome-resolution case for every configured module key.
- **Important files**: `src/app/app/[moduleKey]/layout.tsx` (new), `test/module-team-management.test.ts`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean. `npm run lint` - zero errors, only the same two pre-existing, already-disclosed `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings. `npm run test` - full suite, 164 files/1,248 tests, all passing. `npm run build` - clean, `/app/[moduleKey]/staff` present in the route list.
- **Deployed to production**: pushed to `claude/latest-deployed-updates-bk4j2j`, opened as PR #19 against `main` (no merge conflict). On PR #19's CI, `security` and `validate` were green; `integration` failed, but only on the same pre-existing `test/integration/settlement-activation-lifecycle.test.ts` (`Paystack is not configured (PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY unset)`) already disclosed and confirmed unrelated on every earlier PR today. ## 2026-09-04: Shared team management across operational modules

- **Scope**: added a reusable Team directory and invitation workflow for CRM, Inventory, Procurement, Accounting, Payroll, Analytics, Point of Sale, Projects, Hotel, Pharmacy, and Hospital. Each module now links to `/app/<module>/staff`, where authorized managers can invite staff, assign a supported module role, and activate or suspend access. Read-only module users can view their module team without mutation controls.
- **Identity and boundaries**: the workflow uses the existing `User` and `OrganizationMember` identity model and synchronizes active internal staff into HR. It does not create duplicate staff tables. Role selection is restricted to each module's fixed role family, every query and write is organization-scoped, module access and a module-appropriate management permission are required, platform users are blocked, subscription seats are enforced, self-suspension is blocked, and mutations are audited. POS team mutation remains organization-administrator-only because the current POS Cashier role includes operational settings access and must not be allowed to grant peer access.
- **Specialist exclusions**: Fleet, Installment, Hostel, School, and HR keep their existing specialist staff pages because those workflows own vehicle, customer, building, class, payroll, or employee links that a generic membership page must not bypass.

Full lint passed with zero errors and only the two established PWA hook warnings in `sync-center.tsx` and `pwa-provider.tsx`. The complete unit suite passed 164 files and 1,247 tests. ## 2026-09-04: Fixed the same unfiltered staff-picker bug in Installment (hire-purchase staff login linking)

- **Scope**: user asked to re-check the other modules for the same bug fixed earlier the same day in School and Hostel (every active organization member showing up in a module-specific staff picker, instead of only members who actually belong to that module). Re-ran the audit from scratch across every module's service layer rather than trusting the earlier pass, since the earlier pass had in fact missed one.
- **Found**: `listAssignableStaffUsers` (`src/modules/installment/service.ts`) queried every `ACTIVE` organization member with no permission filter, exactly the same bug shape as School's and Hostel's. It backs the "link a login" picker on `/app/installment/staff` (linking an existing organization member's account to a `HirePurchaseStaff` record).
- **Why this one carries extra weight beyond a confusing dropdown**: the link isn't cosmetic. `resolveInstallmentAccessScope()` (`src/modules/installment/access.ts`) grants a linked user real "staff" self-service scope over their own Installment customers and accounts whenever they lack the organization-wide `hirepurchase.staff.manage` permission. An unfiltered picker meant an operator could link e.g. a Fleet driver's or Hospital radiology staffer's login to a hire-purchase staff profile, handing them Installment data access their actual role never granted - an unintended access-scope bug, not just a confusing list.
- **Fix**: added the same permission-prefix filter used for School and Hostel - only members whose role carries a permission under the `hirepurchase.` prefix now appear. Both the "Hire Purchase Manager" and "Hire Purchase Staff" seeded roles carry `hirepurchase.*` permissions (`prisma/seed-data.ts`), so both remain linkable; unrelated roles (Driver, Radiology Staff, etc.) no longer do.
- **Re-audited the rest of the codebase for the same pattern**, this time grepping every `organizationMember.findMany`/`db.user.findMany` call site directly rather than relying on function-name matching alone: Fleet (already correct), School/Hostel (already fixed the same day), CRM/Projects/HR's owner-assignment pickers (deliberately unfiltered, unchanged), Administration's member list/audit log actor filter/public contact form routing/platform module-request assignee/support online-presence checks (all legitimately organization-wide or already role-scoped to Super Admin, out of scope), subscription-change notifications (broadcast to every member, not a picker), and Hospital's nursing-task `assignedToId` field (no assignee-picker UI exists for it yet - nothing to fix). No other instance of the bug found.
- **Documented**: extended the existing convention section in `docs/MODULE_BOUNDARIES.md` to include Installment's fix and the self-service access-scope reasoning, so a future module-specific staff picker starts from the correct precedent.
- **Important files**: `src/modules/installment/service.ts`, `test/integration/tenant-isolation/installment.test.ts`, `test/installment-ownership.test.ts`, `docs/MODULE_BOUNDARIES.md`.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean. `npm run lint` - zero errors, only the same two pre-existing, already-disclosed `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings. `npm run test` - full suite, 162 files/1,241 tests, all passing (one pre-existing mocked-DB unit test, `installment-ownership.test.ts`'s exact-`where`-clause assertion for `listAssignableStaffUsers`, needed updating to expect the new role filter; updated and reverified). `npm run build` - clean. Added one real-Postgres integration test (`installment.test.ts`), creating a member with the "Hire Purchase Staff" seeded role alongside a Driver-role member, asserting the Driver is excluded and the Hire Purchase Staff member (and the org's Organization Owner) are included - same pattern as the School/Hostel tests, which is the only way this exact filter logic gets executed against real Prisma/Postgres before merge, since this sandbox has no `TEST_DATABASE_URL`.
- **Deployed to production**: pushed to `claude/latest-deployed-updates-bk4j2j`, opened as PR #17 against `main` (no merge conflict - base was already current). On PR #17's CI, `security` and `validate` were green; `integration` failed, but only on the same pre-existing `test/integration/settlement-activation-lifecycle.test.ts` (`Paystack is not configured (PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY unset)`) already disclosed and confirmed unrelated on PRs #15/#16. **The new test this PR added passed for real against Postgres in both the initial run and the one re-run**: `installment.test.ts` 10/10 both times, including "offers only members with Installment access as linkable staff logins, not every active org member". ## 2026-09-04: Fixed module-specific staff pickers showing every organization member (School teachers, Hostel wardens)

- **Scope**: user reported (with a screenshot) that School's "Assign teacher" dropdown on a class listed the organization's Fleet drivers, a Vehicle Owner, an Accounting Manager, Radiology Staff, and the Organization Owner - i.e. every active member of the organization, not people who actually work in School. Asked for this fixed "across all modules."
- **Root cause**: `listOrganizationStaffForAssignment` (`src/modules/school/service.ts`) queried every `ACTIVE` organization member with no filter at all, by original design - its own doc comment said "any active member, not filtered to a 'Teacher'-named role, since scoping is by explicit assignment." That reasoning doesn't hold up: the dropdown is specifically a *class teacher* picker, and showing unrelated staff (drivers, radiology staff) in it is confusing regardless of how the assignment itself is scoped afterward.
- **Fix**: renamed to `listAssignableTeacherUsers` and added a real filter - only members whose role carries a permission under the `school.` prefix now appear, the same prefix test `canAccessModule()` already uses to gate the module itself. There's no single canonical "teacher" permission the way Fleet has one exact permission for driver self-service, so this uses a `startsWith` match on the permission key rather than one exact key.
- **Audited every other "assignable staff" list in the codebase for the same bug**, not just the one reported:
  - **Fleet** (`listAssignableDriverUsers`/`listAssignableOwnerUsers`/`listAssignableMechanicUsers`) was already correctly filtered - by exact permission key for drivers, by exact role name for owners/mechanics. This is the precedent the School and Hostel fixes now follow, and its own doc comment already describes hitting this identical bug once before ("previously let, e.g., the Organization Owner show up as a selectable driver").
  - **Hostel** (`listAssignableHostelUsers`, warden assignment) had the identical unfiltered-list bug. Fixed the same way, filtering on the `hostel.` permission prefix.
  - **CRM** (`listAssignableUsers`/`listActiveMembers`), **Projects** (`listAssignableUsers`), and **HR** (`listContractTemplateResponsibleCandidates`) all list every active member unfiltered too, but deliberately - these pick a genuinely cross-functional "owner" or "responsible party" for a lead, task, or contract, not a module-specific staff role. A CRM deal owner or a project task assignee is not inherently a CRM-permission or Projects-permission holder in the way a class teacher is inherently School staff. Left these unchanged; documented the distinction (see below) so a future change doesn't "fix" them into breaking that.
  - Administration's member list, the audit log's actor list, and the public contact form's operator routing are legitimately organization-wide by design, not module-assignment pickers - out of scope.
- **Documented the convention**: added a new section to `docs/MODULE_BOUNDARIES.md` (after "How this is enforced today") stating the rule - a module-specific staff picker must filter by that module's permission (prefix or exact key), a genuinely cross-functional owner/responsible-party picker deliberately doesn't - so the next module built on this codebase's pattern starts from the correct precedent instead of copying the now-fixed School/Hostel starting point.
- **Important files**: `src/modules/school/service.ts`, `src/app/app/school/classes/page.tsx`, `src/modules/hostel/service.ts`, `test/integration/tenant-isolation/school.test.ts`, `test/integration/tenant-isolation/hostel.test.ts`, `docs/MODULE_BOUNDARIES.md`.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean. `npm run lint` - zero errors, only the same two pre-existing, already-disclosed `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings. `npm run test` - full suite, 160 files/1,237 tests, all passing. `npm run build` - clean, `/app/school/classes` and `/app/hostel/wardens` present. Added one real-Postgres integration test per fixed function (`school.test.ts`, `hostel.test.ts`), each creating a member with the module's own seeded role (Teacher / Warden, both carrying real `school.*`/`hostel.*` permissions per `prisma/seed-data.ts`) alongside a Driver-role member, then asserting the Driver is excluded and the Teacher/Warden (and the org's Organization Owner, who holds every permission) are included. **Could not run these locally**: this environment has no `TEST_DATABASE_URL` configured (a standing limitation disclosed earlier this session for the same reason) - they will run for real against Postgres in CI's `integration` job, which does have that access. The filter logic itself is a direct, minimal copy of Fleet's already-proven, already-shipped pattern (`listAssignableDriverUsers`), which lowers the risk of the untested-locally gap.
- **Deployed to production**: pushed to `claude/latest-deployed-updates-bk4j2j`, opened as PR #15 against `main`. A concurrent session pushed several School UX commits straight to `main` while the PR was open; merged `origin/main` into the branch (`git merge`, the only conflict being the usual `OPERATOR_HANDOFF.md` top-of-file entry, resolved keeping both sessions' content), re-ran the full validation gate against the merged result (`tsc`, lint, full 162-file/1,241-test suite, production build - all clean), and pushed the merge commit. ## 2026-09-04: Redesigned the admin login page (split-screen, animated illustration, real 2FA field)

- **Scope**: user asked for an animated login page for `admin.rockfrostgroup.com` with a 3D illustration on the left and a functional Email/Password form on the right. This went through several rounds first as a standalone HTML mockup (delivered as an Artifact and a downloadable file) to nail the design, using real values pulled from this codebase - the app's actual `oklch()` color tokens, its actual font (Geist, used for every heading and body element via `--font-heading: var(--font-sans)`), the actual 2FA field markup from the real login form, and the real module registry for the module-name chips - rather than inventing a palette or a module list. The user then asked to deploy it, i.e. make this the real `/login` page rather than a separate mockup.
- **Route restructuring**: the login page previously lived at `src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`, sharing `(auth)/layout.tsx` with `/forgot-password`, `/invite`, and `/reset-password` - a centered flex column with the logo above a `max-w-sm` card. A split-screen illustration layout needs the full viewport, so the login route was moved to its own sibling route group, `src/app/(auth-login)/login/page.tsx`, with a minimal `src/app/(auth-login)/layout.tsx` (just metadata, no chrome). The other three auth pages are untouched and still share the original `(auth)/layout.tsx`. The URL is unchanged (`/login`); only the file location and its layout ancestor changed.
- **All real auth behavior preserved verbatim**: `handleSubmit` (bot-protection check, account-lock pre-check, `signIn("credentials", ...)` with `redirect: false`, manual redirect on success, generic invalid-credentials error), `handleSendSmsCode` (the same `requestLoginSmsCode` action, same lock handling), the notice/error message maps read from `searchParams`, the platform-vs-tenant surface banner, and `<TurnstileWidget action="login" />` are all unchanged from the previous page - only the JSX/styling around them changed. No new fields were wired to fake behavior: the earlier standalone mockup had a decorative "Keep me signed in" checkbox and a fake success-checkmark animation on submit; neither exists in the real `signIn` flow, so both were dropped from the real integration rather than shipped as non-functional UI.
- **Design decisions carried over from the mockup, now backed by real data instead of hardcoded values**:
  - Illustration-panel gradient and every color use the app's real `oklch()` custom properties (imported implicitly via Tailwind's `bg-primary`/`text-primary-foreground` etc. utilities where the element is styled with Tailwind, and via literal `oklch(...)` values matching those same tokens in the new CSS module for the parts - the 3D tiles, gradients, keyframes - that are easier to express as plain CSS).
  - The wordmark is the real `<Logo />` component (the actual `/rft.png` asset used everywhere else in the app), placed at the top of the form panel rather than hand-typed on the illustration panel - this was a direct fix for repeated user feedback that a hand-styled "ROCK FROST" / "TECHNOLOGIES" text pairing didn't visually match; using the real logo asset removes the font-matching question entirely rather than tuning weights to approximate it.
  - The 2FA field (`twoFactorCode`, 6-digit numeric, `autoComplete="one-time-code"`, "Send code by SMS") is the exact field from the original page, not a re-creation.
  - The three module-name chips cycle through `catalogueModuleRegistry` (the same array the public marketing pages read from) rather than a hardcoded list, so they can never drift from the real module set. They fade independently and concurrently: each chip steps through a disjoint slice of the module list (slot *i* always advances by 3, so the three chips never show the same module at once) on its own interval (3.6s / 4.2s / 4.8s - slowed down from an initial faster pass per user feedback), each with its own opacity/translateY crossfade.
- **Important files**: `src/app/(auth-login)/login/page.tsx` (new), `src/app/(auth-login)/login/login.module.css` (new), `src/app/(auth-login)/layout.tsx` (new), `src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx` (deleted), `test/security-hardening.test.ts` (path reference updated), `docs/AUTHENTICATION_AND_AUTHORIZATION.md` (path and route-group note updated).
- **Validation**: `rm -rf .next` then `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean (the stale `.next/types` build cache initially referenced the deleted route file; clearing it resolved that). `npm run lint` - zero errors, only the same two pre-existing, already-disclosed `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings, neither in a file this change touched. `npm run test` - full suite, 160 files / 1,237 tests, identical count to before this change, all passing. `npm run build` - clean, no errors or warnings, `/login` present in the route list. Also ran the real dev server and loaded `/login` in a real browser (Playwright): the real `<Logo />` asset, all three real form fields with the exact real 2FA field, and the module chips cycling independently (confirmed two chip layouts several seconds apart showing different, non-overlapping module sets) all render correctly against the actual app, not a mockup. ## 2026-09-03: Fixed live-production UX bug - header connectivity/install badge and trial pill covering the account avatar

- **Scope**: user-reported, screenshot-confirmed bug: the header's "Online"/"Install" connectivity badge (and, whenever visible together with it, the "Subscribed workspace"/"Trial workspace" pill) rendered directly on top of the account avatar in the header's own top-right corner, on the Fleet Owner Workspace page and, since both elements mount globally, on every authenticated page. Pure client-side positioning fix; no schema, permission, or server behavior change.
- **Root cause**: two independent components each use CSS `position: fixed` anchored to the viewport's own top-right corner - `PwaProvider`'s connectivity/update/install badge (`src/components/pwa/pwa-provider.tsx`, `fixed right-3 top-3`) and the trial/subscription-status pill (`src/app/app/layout.tsx`, `fixed right-24 top-4`) - neither aware of the sticky header (`h-16`, 64px tall) that already occupies that same corner with its own controls (module launcher, account avatar). `top-3`/`top-4` (12px/16px from the viewport's top edge) sit squarely inside the header's own 64px height, so whichever of these floats is visible draws over the header's content at a higher z-index. The prior 2026-09-02/03 fix (see below) only silenced the badge when there was nothing to report; it did not change where the badge renders when it does have something to show (an available install prompt, as in the reported screenshot, or offline/update/conflict states) - so the underlying position conflict was never actually resolved, only made rarer.
- **Fix**: moved both floats below the sticky header instead of tuning pixel offsets to dodge the header's current contents (a magic-number fix would silently break again the next time the header's right-hand controls change width, the same class of bug already hit once before with the feedback button/sidebar collision documented in the 2026-09-02/03 entry). Changed `top-3`/`top-4` to `top-20` (80px) on both floats, giving a clean 16px gap below the 64px header regardless of what the header itself contains.
- **Important files**: `src/components/pwa/pwa-provider.tsx`, `src/app/app/layout.tsx`.
- **Validation**: dependencies were not yet installed in this environment; ran `npm ci` first (clean install, 0 vulnerabilities, Prisma Client regenerated). `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean. `npm run lint` - zero errors, only the same two pre-existing, already-disclosed `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings (`sync-center.tsx`, `pwa-provider.tsx`, both untouched by this fix's logic). `npm run test` - full suite passed cleanly on the first run: 160 files, 1,237 tests, no flakiness this run. `npm run build` - passed, all routes generated.
- **Verified visually**: this fix touches only global, always-mounted floats with no per-tenant data, so rather than requiring authenticated session credentials (not available in this environment, a standing limitation disclosed throughout this file's history), verification used a temporary static HTML/CSS reproduction (built and discarded in the scratchpad, never part of the repo) with the exact same Tailwind pixel values as the real classes (`h-16` header, `right-3`/`right-24`, `top-3`/`top-4` before and `top-20` after) rendered via Playwright/Chromium. The "before" screenshot reproduced the reported bug exactly - the badge's white/blue avatar circle sat directly under the "Online"/"Install" pill. The "after" screenshot showed the avatar fully clear, with both floats rendering in an empty band below the header.
- **PR workflow and a pre-existing, unrelated CI failure found and disclosed**: this session operates under a mandatory branch-and-pull-request workflow rather than direct pushes to `main` (unlike the earlier entries below, from sessions that pushed to `main` directly). Commit pushed to `claude/latest-deployed-updates-bk4j2j`; opened as PR #9. This is a standing CI-environment gap (a missing repository secret), not a regression from this change and not fixable from within this PR; disclosed as a PR comment rather than silently worked around. `security` and `validate` (lint, typecheck, full unit suite, production build) both passed cleanly.
- **Deployed and verified in production**: the user asked to merge directly, with no further gate beyond what was already validated (the failing check being the pre-existing, unrelated one above). PR #9 merged into `main` as squash commit `8d68fe0e0712b8092c22af135459c3735887e21e`. Vercel deployment `dpl_96Ycd8Zs39rbJuoyH8a8fQDonDia` reached `READY` and is aliased to `app.rockfrostgroup.com`/`www.rockfrostgroup.com`/`admin.rockfrostgroup.com`/`rockfrostgroup.com`. ## 2026-09-03: Accounting Financial Dashboard (KPI tiles, revenue/P&L trends, ratio benchmarks, period comparison) — deployed and verified

- **Scope**: a new combined `/app/accounting/dashboard` page, modeled on reference dashboards the user shared (Enerpize and a trial Odoo instance): four KPI tiles (Current income, Receivables, Current expense, Payables), a revenue trend chart (Total/Paid/Unpaid/Refund, with an Invoices|Overdue toggle), a Profit & Loss chart (Income/Expenses bars plus a Profit line, with an Accrual|Cash toggle), a Top Invoices list sorted by amount, and 10 financial-ratio "benchmark" gauges (margins, liquidity, solvency, debtor/creditor days) each paired with its formula and original interpretation copy - plus seven period-over-prior-period comparison tables (Cash, Profitability, Performance, Balance sheet, Position, Solvency, Liquidity). No schema change.
- **Deliberate v1 scope limits, disclosed rather than hidden**: Cost of revenue is treated as $0 (no COGS account classification exists), so gross profit margin reads the same as net revenue - matching the reference dashboards' own real behavior. Operating margin equals net profit margin (no operating/non-operating expense split exists). "Current" assets/liabilities means every Asset/Liability account, since the schema has no short-term/long-term classification. Permanence, Financial balance, and Long-term working capital render as "Not available," not a fabricated zero, since all three require that same classification - the reference dashboards show these as 0.00 for their own sample org too, suggesting they're rarely populated even there. Payables (and everything derived from Total Liabilities) reflects only the general ledger's own Accounts Payable account; Procurement's `ProcurementSupplierInvoice` never posts a journal entry, so it has no point-in-time balance history - it IS safely included in the flow-based "credit purchases" figure (a period total, accurate regardless of today's payment status) used for Average payable days, mirroring `getPayablesAgeing`'s existing precedent of merging both sources.
- **Correctness discipline**: KPI tiles reuse `getFinancialComparison`'s current-period values directly rather than `getAccountingSummary` (whose revenue/expense figures are lifetime-since-inception, not period-scoped), so the tiles and the tables beneath them can never disagree. Every ratio uses a shared `computePeriodFinancials` helper computed once per period and reused by both the gauges and the comparison tables, for the same reason. Prior-period comparison uses "to-date vs prior-unit-to-date" (e.g. Sep 1-3 vs Aug 1-3), not a raw duration shift (Sep 1-3 vs Aug 29-31), which would produce a near-empty, misleading window on day 3 of a new period.
- **Important files**: `src/modules/accounting/dashboard-service.ts` (new), two small additive changes to `src/modules/accounting/service.ts` (`getAccountBalancesAsOf`, a point-in-time balance snapshot; `getCashFlowStatement` gains gross `cashReceived`/`cashSpent` fields alongside its existing net figures), `src/components/dashboard/charts.tsx` (new `GaugeChart` and `ComposedTrendChart`/`PeriodicComposedTrendChart`), `src/app/app/accounting/dashboard/page.tsx` and `dashboard-toggles.tsx` (new), `src/modules/accounting/navigation.tsx` and `src/app/app/accounting/page.tsx` (nav entry and cross-link), `docs/DASHBOARD_KPI_STANDARD.md` (new KPI table for this dashboard, following the School table's format).
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm run lint` zero new warnings (the two pre-existing, already-disclosed `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings remain). New `test/accounting-financial-dashboard.test.ts` (7 tests) checks every ratio formula against a hand-computed fixture (Total Assets 42,000; Total Liabilities 15,000; Total Equity 27,000; Revenue 25,000; Expenses 18,000 - verified `42,000 = 15,000 + 27,000`) and confirms zero-denominator ratios render `null` rather than `Infinity`/`NaN`; extended `test/accounting-reporting.test.ts` covers the two `service.ts` additions directly. Full unit suite passed (1,237 tests, the two well-established pre-existing load-induced timeouts in `ai-support-assistant.test.ts`/`fleet-owner-workspace.test.ts` the only exceptions, both previously confirmed passing in isolation repeatedly this session). Verified live via a temporary scratch route (removed before finishing) rendering the real `GaugeChart`, `RevenueTrendSection`, and `ProfitLossSection` components with fixture data: KPI tiles, both chart toggles (confirmed switching series client-side with no network request), the accessible data tables, and all sample gauges rendered correctly with no console errors.
- **A real bug caught and fixed during validation**: the null/"no value" placeholder in `formatRow`/`formatDelta`/`buildGauge`/the Top Invoices "Created by" column initially used a literal em dash (`—`), the exact anti-pattern `test/editorial-punctuation.test.ts` exists to catch (added after a real prior production incident with this same pattern). Replaced with the spelled-out "Not available" throughout.
- **Deployed and verified in production**: this feature was committed alongside unrelated, independently-developed School work (`1d60a7a`, `ac9d178`) already documented in the entry above - the shared working tree combined both features into the same commits. Production deployment `dpl_EUCMp2bz7YCHdeGoQ272VzmXKhbh` (commit `1d60a7a`) reached `READY`. Production `get_runtime_errors` (last 1h) showed no errors attributable to this feature - every reported error was in the unrelated School Sharp-packaging issue, already fixed in `ac9d178`. Unauthenticated `GET /app/accounting/dashboard` correctly redirected to `/login`, matching every other Accounting reporting page's permission gate. A small follow-up commit (`d7d739d`) fixed one test assertion left referencing the old em-dash placeholder after the fix above landed.

## 2026-09-02/03: Fixed two live-production UX bugs (session-expired banner stuck permanently, feedback button overlapping the sidebar) — deployed and verified

- **Scope**: an urgent, user-reported live-production report with a screenshot: a persistent "Offline session expired. Local access was cleared." pill sat over the header, covering the profile avatar, with no way to dismiss it; and the "Share feedback" button overlapped the sidebar's own "Collapse sidebar" control at the bottom-left corner. Both are pure client-side UX/positioning fixes; neither changes any server behavior, schema, or permission.
- **Root cause 1 (session-expired banner)**: `PwaProvider` (`src/components/pwa/pwa-provider.tsx`) treated any non-2xx response from `/api/offline/devices` registration the same as a `401`, setting `sessionExpired` permanently with no reset path. Today's own platform-level offline-access-grant work (see the `2026-09-02: Organization offline access` track) made the endpoint return `403 offline-disabled` for every organization not yet granted platform access - effectively all of them today - so the misclassification, though pre-existing, was newly and universally triggered. Fix: only a genuine `401` sets `sessionExpired`; other non-OK statuses (including the expected `403`) are ignored.
- **Root cause 2 (feedback button overlap)**: `WorkspaceMoments` (`src/components/feedback/workspace-moments.tsx`) and `AppShell`'s sidebar footer both independently target the same `fixed bottom-left` viewport corner with no coordination between the two files. Fix: added `lg:left-72` to the feedback button's fixed container, clearing the sidebar's up-to-16rem width (expanded or collapsed) on desktop, where the sidebar is a persistent column. Below `lg`, the sidebar is a slide-out sheet instead, so the original corner position is unchanged there.
- **Second, related fix while in this file anyway**: the connectivity status pill itself (same component) was rendered unconditionally, meaning even the ordinary "Online" state permanently occupied the header's top-right corner - the same corner the account/avatar menu occupies. Changed to render only when there is something to report: `state !== "online" || Boolean(installPrompt)`. Silent in the common case; still shows for offline, syncing, conflict, update-available, or install-prompt states.
- **Important files**: `src/components/pwa/pwa-provider.tsx`, `src/components/feedback/workspace-moments.tsx`, `test/offline-pwa.test.ts` (+2), `test/workspace-moments.test.ts` (+1 describe block).
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` on the changed files - clean. `npm run lint` - zero new warnings (the two pre-existing, unrelated `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings in `sync-center.tsx`/`pwa-provider.tsx` remain, already disclosed). Targeted tests - 17/17 passing across both files. Verified live via a temporary scratch route (removed before committing, never shipped) replicating the real sidebar width, header avatar position, and both fixed-position components: confirmed no badge renders in the "online" state; confirmed the badge renders without overlapping the avatar in "offline" and "conflict" states; confirmed the feedback button renders clear of the sidebar's collapse control in both states.
- **Temporarily blocked before production, per CLAUDE.md's "stop before production if a required gate fails or safe deployment is blocked" and the user's explicit instruction to leave unrelated concurrent work untouched**: a second agent had an active, uncommitted "Student 360 and Digital ID" school feature in the same shared working tree (`src/app/app/school/students/[studentId]/page.tsx`, `src/app/verify/student-id/[publicId]/page.tsx`, and related files), with real, unrelated TypeScript errors that a plain local `npm run build` in that shared directory would pick up. This fix was committed locally only, as `f1b8acd`, and withheld from `git push` while that work was in progress. No school/verify file was ever read for editing purposes or modified.
- **How the block was actually resolved**: since the other agent's files were uncommitted (confirmed via `git status`), `git push` was never going to include them regardless of their state - only `git`-tracked commit history reaches Vercel, not the shared working directory's disk contents. The correct isolation check was therefore a clean, disposable `git worktree add --detach` at this fix's own commit (`9d9c559`, built on the previously-deployed `a40ff82`, touching only the two component files, their tests, and this doc), run entirely separately from the shared directory. Notably, `module-access.test.ts`'s guarded-file-count assertion - which fails in the shared working directory because it picks up the other agent's uncommitted new page - passed cleanly here, confirming the isolated checkout was the right thing to validate.
- **Deployed and verified in production**: `git push origin main` (`9d9c559`, carrying `f1b8acd` and the accompanying docs commit). ## 2026-09-02: Platform owner can mark a product available or unavailable in the catalogue

- **Scope**: the platform owner asked, while looking at the live `/app/platform/modules` page, for a toggle to mark a module available or not. `Module.status` (`ACTIVE | INACTIVE | COMING_SOON`) already existed as a real column and already gated five real consumers - new subscription creation (`platform/subscriptions/service.ts`), the org detail page's own module enable/configure list, the tenant self-service "request a module" page, the platform's own request-handling page, and the public contact form's module matching - but nothing in the app had ever set it to anything other than `ACTIVE`, since there was no UI to change it.
- **Deliberately distinct from `toggleOrganizationModule`**: that existing action (per-org `OrganizationModule.enabled`, toggled from an org's own detail page) is untouched by this track. This new toggle changes only the catalogue-level `Module.status` row - an organization that already has a module enabled keeps working exactly as before regardless of what the platform owner does here. Marking a module unavailable only stops it from being offered to anyone new; it does not touch any existing organization's access.
- **New action**: `toggleModuleAvailability()` (`src/app/app/platform/modules/actions.ts`), gated on `isPlatformOperator` exactly like `toggleOrganizationModule()`, sets `status: "ACTIVE"` or `"INACTIVE"` and logs `module.marked_available`/`module.marked_unavailable`. Deliberately never sets `COMING_SOON` - that third state means "not yet launched," a different concept from "temporarily paused," and isn't reachable from this simple on/off control (a currently-`COMING_SOON` product can still be switched straight to `ACTIVE` to launch it, since the toggle's own "on" state always means `ACTIVE`).
- **Badge fix while touching this code anyway**: the page's status badge previously collapsed `COMING_SOON` and a would-be `INACTIVE` into the identical "Coming soon" label (`mod.status === "ACTIVE" ? "Available" : "Coming soon"`). Replaced with a proper three-state map so "Unavailable" now reads honestly as unavailable rather than "coming soon."

## 2026-09-02: Fixed the pre-existing offline-module-adapters type error

- **Scope**: closes the one pre-existing, unrelated issue disclosed (twice) in the previous two tracks - a type-only fix, no behavior change, no schema change, no UI to verify live.
- **Root cause**: `applyOfflineModuleOperation()` (`src/lib/pwa/server-adapters.ts`) declared its internal `result` variable as a bare `Record<string, unknown>`, then returned `{ ...result, serverTimestamp: ... }`. TypeScript's object-spread type inference drops a plain index signature entirely when computing the resulting object literal's type - so the function's real, always-present `status` field (every one of its seven branches sets it) silently vanished from the *inferred return type*, even though the actual runtime object always had it. `test/integration/offline-module-adapters.test.ts` accessing `result.status` was the only place this surfaced as a compile error, since it's the only caller that reads the field with a bare property access rather than through the JSON `NextResponse` boundary (which erases types anyway).
- **Fix**: typed `result` as `{ status: string } & Record<string, unknown>` instead - an intersection with a named property is preserved through the spread, and every branch's assignment already satisfies it (each sets a real string-typed `status`, confirmed for all seven branches before making the change). Purely a type annotation; the object built and returned at runtime is byte-for-byte identical to before.
- **Important files**: `src/lib/pwa/server-adapters.ts` (one function, one variable declaration changed plus a comment explaining why).
- **Validation**: `npx prisma format`/`validate` - not applicable, no schema touched. `npx tsc --noEmit` - fully clean, zero errors anywhere in the repository (the last remaining error is gone). `npm run lint` - zero errors; the same two pre-existing `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings in `sync-center.tsx`/`pwa-provider.tsx` remain, both untouched by this fix and already disclosed. `npm run test` - passed: full suite 155 of 157 files, the 2 failures (`ai-support-assistant.test.ts`, `fleet-owner-workspace.test.ts`) the exact same well-established pre-existing load-induced timeout flakiness confirmed repeatedly earlier today, not re-verified in isolation again since already proven multiple times. `npm run build` - passed.
- **Not separately re-run**: `test/integration/offline-module-adapters.test.ts` itself (the test whose compile error this fixes) requires `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, not configured in this environment - the same standing limitation disclosed throughout this repository's history. Its compile-time correctness is confirmed by the now-clean `tsc --noEmit`; its runtime behavior was never in question, since the fix changes no runtime logic.
- **Deployed and verified in production**: no schema change, so `git push origin main` (`2624df0`) directly, no migration step. Vercel deployment `dpl_AEaUiBUTQbnvHyppC1kEeTEC1CkG` reached `READY` and is aliased to `app.rockfrostgroup.com`. Post-deploy checks: `get_runtime_errors` (last 30m) - none found; `GET /api/health` - `200 {"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. No route-specific check needed - this fix touches no route and changes no runtime behavior.

## 2026-09-02: Platform owner gains a master switch over which organizations get offline access

- **Scope**: the user asked for "a lot more control and functions" for the platform owner, naming "which organization gets offline access" as the concrete example. Investigation found offline access was entirely tenant self-service - any organization's own Owner could enable browser offline capability, choose its modules, set the lease length, and even turn off the mutation kill switch, all via `updateOfflineAccessSettings()` (`src/app/app/(overview)/organization/settings/actions.ts`), with zero platform-owner visibility or control. This directly contradicted the offline platform's own documented release boundary ("Organization policies default closed and the mutation kill switch defaults on, so deployment does not silently enable offline capture for any tenant" and "until an operator deliberately enables a tenant" - see this file's own 2026-09-01 "Guarded browser PWA and POS offline phase released" and "Browser PWA guarded release candidate validated" entries). This track closes that gap with a platform-level master switch, mirroring the existing `OrganizationModule.enabled` (platform-controlled) plus `configuration` (tenant-fine-tuned) pattern already used for every other module.
- **Schema**: `Organization` gains `offlineAccessGranted` (`Boolean @default(false)`), `offlineAccessGrantedAt` (`DateTime?`), `offlineAccessGrantedById` (`String?`, a plain audit-trail id with no FK relation, matching the existing `deletionRequestedById` convention on the same model). Migration `20260902100000_organization_offline_access_grant` is purely additive - three new nullable/defaulted columns, no existing row touched. Every organization defaults ungranted, the correct fail-closed default for a feature whose own documented history confirms no real organization has completed a production offline canary yet - so no backfill was needed or attempted.
- **Enforcement**: `/api/offline/devices`'s `POST` handler (the sole point where a browser device registers for offline capability) now refuses registration with `403 offline-disabled` unless `organization.offlineAccessGranted` is true, in addition to the pre-existing check that the organization's own self-service policy (`resolveOfflinePolicy()`) has `enabled: true`. Both must be true - the platform grant does not itself turn offline on for an organization that hasn't configured it, and the organization's own configuration has no effect until the platform grants it. This is the only enforcement chokepoint that needed changing: every other offline route (`sync`, `conflicts`, `attachments`, `work-packs`) authorizes off the already-registered `OfflineDevice`'s own stored `offlineAccessUntil`/`moduleKeys`, not a live policy re-resolution, so revoking a grant takes effect on that device's next registration/refresh (bounded by its lease, 1-24 hours) - the same latency characteristic every existing policy change already has, not a new gap introduced here.
- **Platform UI**: a new "Offline access" card on `/app/platform/organizations/[organizationId]`, between Modules and Recent requests. Shows Granted/Not granted with a timestamp when granted, a toggle (`OfflineAccessToggle`, mirroring `ModuleToggle`'s exact optimistic-update pattern), and a read-only summary of the organization's own self-service configuration (enabled/lease/kill-switch/requested modules) so the platform owner can see what a tenant has configured even before deciding whether to grant it.
- **New action**: `toggleOrganizationOfflineAccess()` (`src/app/app/platform/actions.ts`), gated on `isPlatformOperator` exactly like the existing `toggleOrganizationModule()`, stamping `offlineAccessGrantedAt`/`offlineAccessGrantedById` on grant and clearing both on revoke (not just flipping a flag), and logging `offline_access.platform_granted`/`offline_access.platform_revoked` audit events.
- **A process-discipline lesson, not a code defect**: after editing `prisma/schema.prisma`, `npx prisma format` and `npx prisma validate` were run but `npx prisma generate` was not - so the first `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` passes ran against a stale Prisma Client that didn't yet know about the new `Organization` fields, and passed cleanly for the wrong reason. Only `npm run build`'s own type-check caught the real error (`offlineAccessGranted` not found on `OrganizationSelect`) since Next's build pipeline forces a fresh client. Fixed by running `npx prisma generate` before re-verifying; `prisma format`/`validate` alone are not sufficient confirmation after a schema edit, `generate` must run too before trusting a `tsc` pass. Recorded here so this exact gap doesn't recur on a future schema-changing track.
- **A pre-existing, unrelated issue found and deliberately left unfixed**: `npx tsc --noEmit` reports one type error in `test/integration/offline-module-adapters.test.ts` (`applyOfflineModuleOperation`'s return type loses its literal `status` key through a `Record<string, unknown>` spread in `src/lib/pwa/server-adapters.ts`, a file this track never touched). Confirmed non-blocking - `npm run build` compiled clean in this same track since Next's build type-check doesn't reach test files - and confirmed low-urgency, since this guarded integration test requires `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, not configured in this environment, so it never actually runs here regardless. Left out of this track's scope; flagged to the user rather than silently fixed.
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260902100000_organization_offline_access_grant/`, `src/app/api/offline/devices/route.ts`, `src/app/app/platform/actions.ts`, `src/app/app/platform/organizations/offline-access-toggle.tsx` (new), `src/app/app/platform/organizations/[organizationId]/page.tsx`, `test/platform-offline-access-grant.test.ts` (new), `test/offline-pwa.test.ts`.
- **Validation**: `npx prisma format`/`validate`/`generate` - passed. `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean for every file this track touched (the one pre-existing, unrelated error noted above remains and is untouched). `npm run lint` - passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` - passed: targeted (`platform-offline-access-grant.test.ts` + `offline-pwa.test.ts`) 2 files/15 tests clean on the first run; full suite 151 of 154 files passing, the 3 failures (`ai-support-assistant.test.ts`, `fleet-owner-workspace.test.ts`, `editorial-punctuation.test.ts`) all confirmed the same pre-existing, load-induced timeout flakiness already extensively documented in this file's prior entries - all 3 passed cleanly (25 tests) when re-run together in isolation. `npm run build` - passed after regenerating the Prisma Client, all 242 routes present, no scratch route.
- **Verified live in a browser** with a temporary scratch route (removed before shipping) rendering the real `OfflineAccessToggle` component and the exact "Offline access" card markup twice, with fixture data for an ungranted and a granted organization: the ungranted card showed "Not granted," its toggle off, and the organization's own (also-disabled) configuration; the granted card showed "Granted 02/09/2026, 10:00:00 am," its toggle on, and the organization's own configured lease/modules/kill-switch state - confirmed via both the rendered accessibility tree and a screenshot.
- **Deployed and verified in production**: purely additive migration, no data-shape risk to check beforehand, so `npx prisma migrate deploy && git push origin main` ran unpiped directly (`ab43a8f`), migration `20260902100000_organization_offline_access_grant` applied cleanly. Vercel deployment `dpl_4uxPKaj5TfHLxmZqpJea98fdy9rd` reached `READY` and is aliased to `app.rockfrostgroup.com`. Post-deploy checks: `get_runtime_errors` (last 30m) - none found; `GET /api/health` - `200 {"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`; unauthenticated `GET /app/platform/organizations` - `307` to `/login`; unauthenticated `POST /api/offline/devices` - `401`, confirming the pre-existing auth guard is intact alongside the new platform-grant gate sitting behind it.

## 2026-09-01: Hotfix - AccountingAttachment.branchId missing from production database

- **Scope**: fixes a live production crash on `/app/accounting/bills` (and any other page listing Accounting attachments), discovered incidentally while verifying an unrelated sidebar change. `AccountingAttachment.branch`/`branchId` has been declared in `prisma/schema.prisma` since Track 12's very first commit (`3b13581`), but Track 12's migration (`20260901100000_accounting_attachments`) never actually added the column to the database - a migration-authorship gap, not a design change. Every `db.accountingAttachment.findMany()` call (the Prisma client selects every scalar field by default) has been throwing `PrismaClientKnownRequestError P2022: The column AccountingAttachment.branchId does not exist in the current database` since that deployment.
- **Confirmed safe to add, not to remove**: `createAccountingAttachment()` never writes to `AccountingAttachment.branchId` (only to `FileAsset.branchId`, a distinct, pre-existing, already-correct column on a different table) - so the fix is purely catching the database up to schema/application code that has been correct all along, not a new feature or a behavior change.
- **Schema**: new migration `20260901120000_accounting_attachment_branch_scope` adds one nullable column (`branchId TEXT`), its index, and its FK to `Branch` (`ON DELETE SET NULL ON UPDATE CASCADE`, matching `FileAsset.branchId`'s own existing FK exactly). Purely additive - no existing row is touched, no data-shape risk. Confirmed via `npx prisma migrate status` against production that this is the only pending migration and local history matches the database's applied set (aside from three pre-baseline migration files not present locally, a pre-existing, unrelated artifact of this repo's migration history).
- **Important files**: `prisma/migrations/20260901120000_accounting_attachment_branch_scope/migration.sql` (new). No application code changes - `schema.prisma` and every TypeScript call site were already correct.
- **Validation**: `npx prisma format` - passed. `npx prisma validate` - passed. `npx prisma migrate status` - confirmed exactly one pending migration, matching this fix precisely. No test/build changes needed since no application code changed; the full suite and production build were already confirmed passing earlier in this same session (151 files, 1215 tests; `npm run build` clean) before this bug was found.
- **Deployed and verified in production**: purely additive migration, no data-shape risk to check beforehand, so `npx prisma migrate deploy && git push origin main` ran unpiped directly (`6b17e75`), migration `20260901120000_accounting_attachment_branch_scope` applied cleanly. Post-deploy checks: `get_runtime_errors` (last 15m) - none found, and no new P2022 on `AccountingAttachment.branchId` in particular; `GET /api/health` - `200 {"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`; unauthenticated `GET /app/accounting/bills` - `307` to `/login` as expected. The unauthenticated redirect fires before the page's own data fetch, so it does not by itself prove an authenticated attachment-list query now succeeds - no authenticated test-tenant credentials exist in this environment, the same standing limitation disclosed throughout this repository's history.
