## 2026-09-01: Ghana tax completion, Fleet/Accounting redesign Track 13 of 14

- **Scope**: Track 13. Withholding tax on bill payments, tax-inclusive pricing calculation, a currency default fix for new organizations, and Ghana-formatted printable invoice/bill PDFs.
- **Schema**: `AccountingTaxCode` gains `withholdingRate` (default 0) and an optional `withholdingCategory` (`GOODS | SERVICES | RENT`). `AccountingPayablePayment` gains `withholdingTaxAmount`. `AccountingInvoice`/`AccountingBill` gain `taxInclusive` (default `false`). `Organization.currency`'s default changes from `USD` to `GHS` (forward-only - a `DEFAULT` clause only ever applies to a new row with no explicit value). `2130 Withholding Tax Payable` joins the 12 guaranteed system accounts (13 now); its former, redundant `2200` entry was removed from the optional Ghana SME chart-of-accounts template accordingly (21 template accounts down to 20) - an org that already loaded the template keeps its own existing `2200` row. Migration `20260901110000_ghana_tax_completion` is purely additive.
- **Withholding tax**: applied in `recordBillPayment()` - when the bill's tax code has a configured `withholdingRate`, the cash actually paid is the payment amount net of the withheld portion, credited instead to `2130 Withholding Tax Payable`; `amountPaid` still increments by the full payment amount, since the payable is satisfied partly in cash and partly by tax withheld on the supplier's behalf. Every bill with no configured withholding rate - every bill that existed before this feature - posts the identical two-line entry as always; this is additive-only.
- **A real bug caught before shipping**: the first draft gated the withholding-tax code path on `Prisma.Decimal.isPositive()`, which returns `true` for exactly zero (decimal.js's `isPositive` means "non-negative," not "strictly greater than zero"). Every bill payment, including every one with no withholding configured, would have posted a spurious three-line entry with a GHS 0.00 credit to Withholding Tax Payable. The track's own regression-guard test caught this before any commit; fixed with `.greaterThan(0)`.
- **Tax-inclusive pricing**: `calculateTaxInclusive()` back-calculates the taxable amount from a gross amount that already includes VAT/NHIL/GETFund, with `getfundAmount` absorbing any rounding remainder so the four figures always reconcile exactly to the gross amount. Matches `calculateTax()`'s own forward calculation exactly on the same underlying taxable amount. The schema flag is in place; wiring it into the Invoice/Bill creation UI is left for those pages' own future iteration - the same "service ready, one UI wired" shape Track 11 and 12 both used.
- **Printable documents**: `buildPrintableDocumentPdf()` (a new, document-style PDF distinct from the existing tabular `buildReportPdf`) renders a letterhead, counterparty block, line-item table, and VAT/NHIL/GETFund breakdown, with Ghana-conventional `DD/MM/YYYY` dates. Served by a new bespoke route, `/api/accounting/documents/[type]?id=...` for `invoice`/`bill`; a paid document's own totals block doubles as its receipt, so no third template was needed. "Print" links added to the Invoices and Bills pages.
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260901110000_ghana_tax_completion/`, `src/lib/reports/invoice-pdf.ts` (new), `src/app/api/accounting/documents/[type]/route.ts` (new), `src/modules/accounting/service.ts`, `src/modules/accounting/tax-service.ts`, `src/app/app/accounting/tax/{page.tsx,actions.ts}`, `src/app/app/accounting/{invoices,bills}/page.tsx`, `docs/ACCOUNTING_MODULE.md`, `test/accounting-ghana-tax.test.ts` (new), `test/invoice-pdf.test.ts` (new), `test/integration/tenant-isolation/organization-currency-default.test.ts` (new), `test/accounting-reporting.test.ts` (updated account code lists).

## 2026-09-01: Recurring transactions, Fleet/Accounting redesign Track 11 of 14

- **Scope**: Track 11. New `AccountingRecurringTemplate` model, a shared generation dispatch path used identically by a new authenticated cron sweep and a manual "run now" catch-up action, and UI on the Journal page to create/pause/resume/run recurring journal-entry templates.
- **Schema**: `AccountingRecurringTemplate` (`type: JOURNAL_ENTRY | INVOICE | BILL`, `frequency: WEEKLY | MONTHLY | QUARTERLY | YEARLY`, `nextRunDate`, a discriminated-by-type `payload` JSON column, `active`, `lastGeneratedAt`). Migration `20260831200000_accounting_recurring_templates` is purely additive - one new table, no changes to any existing column.
- **Service**: `generateFromTemplate()` is the single dispatch path both the cron sweep and manual run-now call, guaranteeing they produce the same result - `entryDate`/`issueDate`/`billDate` always comes from the template's own `nextRunDate`, never "today," so a late catch-up run still books on the date it was actually due. `generateDueRecurringTransactions(now)` (cron entry point, spans every organization) generates each due template's document and only then advances `nextRunDate` - generate-then-advance means a failed generation never silently advances the schedule and skips a period. One template's failure is isolated and reported in a `failures` list, never thrown, so the sweep keeps processing every other due template. `runRecurringTemplateNow()` reuses the identical generate-then-advance logic keyed by template id instead of by due date.
- **Cron**: `/api/cron/recurring-transactions` (`vercel.json`, `30 1 * * *`) follows the exact `CRON_SECRET`/`timingSafeEqual`/correlation-id-logging pattern already proven by `expire-trials` and `appointment-reminders`. A per-template failure inside the sweep still returns `200` with a `failed` count (plus a separate error-level log line) - the endpoint did its job even when one template's document couldn't be generated.
- **UI scope**: the Journal page gained "New recurring entry," a "Recurring templates" list (frequency, next/last-run dates, Active/Paused badge, Pause/Resume, Run now), wired for the `JOURNAL_ENTRY` type specifically, mirroring the page's own existing 2-line debit/credit manual-entry form. `INVOICE`/`BILL` recurrence is fully supported by the same schema and service functions, ready for the Invoices and Bills pages to add their own template UI on top of the identical service layer.
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260831200000_accounting_recurring_templates/`, `vercel.json`, `src/app/api/cron/recurring-transactions/route.ts` (new), `src/modules/accounting/service.ts`, `src/app/app/accounting/journal/{page.tsx,actions.ts}`, `docs/ACCOUNTING_MODULE.md`, `test/accounting-recurring-transactions.test.ts` (new), `test/recurring-transactions-cron.test.ts` (new).

- **Reordering note**: the plan's Track 12 was going to introduce the shared CSV-parsing primitive that Track 10's bank-statement import depends on. Rather than build bank reconciliation on a primitive that doesn't exist yet, `src/lib/csv-import.ts` (using the `csv-parse` package, a real dependency) was built now as part of this track; Track 12 will extend/reuse it for Chart-of-Accounts and Contacts import without redoing the parser.
- **Schema**: new `AccountingBankStatementLineStatus` enum (`UNMATCHED | MATCHED | IGNORED`) and `AccountingBankStatementLine` model (date, description, signed `amount`, `sequenceInFile`, optional `matchedJournalLineId`). `@@unique([reconciliationId, sequenceInFile])` is the idempotent-re-import key: re-uploading the same file re-parses to the same row-to-sequence mapping, so `createMany({skipDuplicates: true})` silently skips every row the second time. Migration `20260831190000_accounting_bank_statement_reconciliation` is purely additive - one new table, no changes to any existing column.
- **Service**: `createDraftReconciliation()` creates (or returns the existing) `DRAFT` `AccountingReconciliation` for an account/period - the schema's `DRAFT` status existed already but no code path had ever produced one. `importBankStatementLines()`, `suggestReconciliationMatches()` (exact-amount match preferred, falling back to a 0.01 tolerance only when no exact match exists, within a 3-day date pad, computed fresh on every call so a suggestion can never go stale), `confirmReconciliationMatch()`, `ignoreReconciliationLine()`, and `completeDraftReconciliation()` (identical `statementBalance - ledgerBalance` math to the existing `completeReconciliation()`, which is untouched). An unmatched line was never posted anywhere, so it simply keeps the difference non-zero until a human resolves it.
- **UI**: Cash and bank gains a "Start import" form creating the draft and redirecting into a new reconciliation workspace (`/app/accounting/reconciliations/[reconciliationId]`) with the CSV upload, suggested-match confirm/ignore controls, and the completion form; the Reconciliation history list shows an in-progress draft with a "Resume" link instead of a misleading zero-difference "Balanced" badge.

## 2026-08-31: Journal entry approval workflow, Fleet/Accounting redesign Track 9 of 14

- **Scope**: Track 9. A manual journal entry created by someone without the new `accounting.journal.approve` permission now lands `PENDING_APPROVAL` instead of posting immediately, and has zero effect on any account balance until a separate approver reviews it. An actor who already holds the permission still posts immediately, exactly as before this track.
- **Schema**: `AccountingJournalStatus` gains two additive values, `PENDING_APPROVAL` and `REJECTED`, alongside the existing `POSTED`/`REVERSED`. `AccountingJournalEntry` gains `submittedById`, `approvedById`, `approvedAt`, `rejectedReason`. Migration `20260831180000_accounting_journal_approval` combines the enum-value additions and the column additions in one migration (the established precedent from `20260831140000_fleet_maintenance_external_repairs`): no DML in the migration itself uses either new enum value, so it can't collide with Postgres's add-then-use-in-a-later-transaction rule.
- **New permission**: `accounting.journal.approve`, added to `ALL_PERMISSIONS` (so Organization Owner/Admin/Super Admin already have it) and to the "Accounting Manager" role's permission list.
- **Service**: `createManualJournalEntry()` takes a new `requiresApproval` boolean, set by the Action layer from the actor's own permission (the service layer has no permission context of its own) - `true` creates the entry `PENDING_APPROVAL` with `submittedById` set; omitted/`false` posts `POSTED` immediately, unchanged from before this track. New `approveJournalEntry()`/`rejectJournalEntry()` mirror the Planning module's proven approval-state-machine: an optimistic `updateMany` scoped to `status: "PENDING_APPROVAL"` claims the transition, and the submitter cannot approve their own entry (rejecting your own submission is allowed, matching Planning's own asymmetry). Every account-balance-affecting read - `listAccounts()`, `getCashbook()`, `getTrialBalance()`, `getGeneralLedgerForAccount()`, and both queries inside `getCashFlowStatement()` - now filters journal lines to exclude `PENDING_APPROVAL`/`REJECTED` via one shared `NON_POSTED_JOURNAL_STATUSES` constant; `POSTED` and `REVERSED` both stay included since a reversal's original lines and its compensating entry only net to zero together.
- **UI**: `/app/accounting/journal` shows an amber "Awaiting approval" note on pending entries and a "Rejected: {reason}" note on rejected ones. Approve/Reject controls appear only for an approver who is not the entry's own submitter, enforced independently in both the UI and the service layer.
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260831180000_accounting_journal_approval/`, `src/modules/accounting/service.ts`, `src/lib/auth/permissions.ts`, `prisma/seed-data.ts`, `src/app/app/accounting/journal/{page.tsx,actions.ts}`, `docs/ACCOUNTING_MODULE.md`, `test/accounting-journal-approval.test.ts` (new).
- **Validation**: `npx prisma format`/`generate` - passed. `npx tsc --noEmit` - passed. `npm run lint` - passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` - passed: 140 files (+1 new), 1139 tests (+14 net new: immediate-post regression guard, pending-lands-not-posted, approve happy path, submitter-cannot-approve-own, approve/reject on a non-pending entry, reject requires a reason, and a query-shape assertion per balance-affecting read site confirming the status exclusion filter). `npm run build` - passed.
- **Verified live in a browser** with a temporary scratch route (removed before shipping) rendering the Journal page's new UI states with fixture data: a posted entry (Reverse control only), a pending entry submitted by someone else (Approve/Reject controls visible), a pending entry submitted by the viewer themselves (controls correctly hidden), and a rejected entry (reason displayed).
- **Deployed and verified in production**: `npx prisma migrate deploy && git push origin main` run unpiped (`9e823bb`), migration `20260831180000_accounting_journal_approval` applied cleanly (purely additive - two new enum values, four new nullable columns - no backfill or data-shape risk, so no pre-migration read-only safety check was needed). The production seed log confirmed the new permission propagated correctly (Accounting Manager gained a 20th permission grant; Organization Admin's grant count rose to 169, i.e. all 170 permissions minus `org.settings.manage`). ## 2026-08-31: Accounting reporting suite, Fleet/Accounting redesign Track 8 of 14

- **Scope**: Track 8. Adds the reporting suite that was conspicuously absent despite the ledger data already existing cleanly for it: trial balance, general ledger, real AR/AP ageing buckets, a direct-method cash-flow statement, and a Ghana SME chart-of-accounts template. No schema change - every report is a pure read/compute over existing data.
- **Trial balance**: `getTrialBalance()` sums each account's raw debit-minus-credit as of a date and shows it in whichever column the sign falls on - not normalized by type - so the debit-column total always equals the credit-column total by construction (`/app/accounting/trial-balance`).
- **General ledger**: a new index page (reusing `listAccounts()`'s existing balance computation) linking into a per-account page showing every journal line ever posted against it, oldest first, with a running balance (`/app/accounting/general-ledger`, `/app/accounting/general-ledger/[accountId]`).
- **AR/AP ageing**: real current/1-30/31-60/61-90/90+ day buckets (`/app/accounting/ageing`), replacing the only prior avenue for understanding ageing (the Receivables page's binary current/overdue flag, left as-is since it serves a different statement-style purpose). Payables ageing reads both `AccountingBill` and Procurement's `ProcurementSupplierInvoice` (through Procurement's own exported `listSupplierInvoices()`, not a direct table query) so the payable position is complete regardless of which flow created the obligation.
- **Cash-flow statement**: direct method (`/app/accounting/cash-flow`) - every cash/bank/mobile-money journal line in a date range, categorized Operating/Investing/Financing by source type (everything today is legitimately Operating; no fixed-asset or loan module exists yet to originate the other two). `openingCash + netChange = closingCash` by construction.
- **Ghana SME chart-of-accounts template**: a "Load Ghana SME chart of accounts" button on the Chart of Accounts page upserts 21 additional Ghana-flavored accounts by code (Bank, Mobile Money, Withholding Tax Payable, Owner's Capital, Salaries and Wages, Rent, Utilities, and more), skipping anything already present and never colliding with the 12 system-managed accounts every org already has.
- **Export**: all four new reports export to PDF/XLSX through one new bespoke route (`/api/reports/accounting/[reportType]`), mirroring the Fleet owner statement's existing bespoke-route pattern (real per-row data, not the generic summary-card flatten every plain module Reports page export uses).

## 2026-08-31: Accounting contacts, multi-line invoices, bills, and credit notes, Fleet/Accounting redesign Track 7 of 14

- **Scope**: Track 7. First track focused on the Accounting module itself. Adds a shared customer/supplier contact record, converts invoices from a single freeform amount to real line items, and adds two new first-class document types: standalone Bills (payables without a purchase order) and Credit Notes.
- **Schema**: new `AccountingContact` (type CUSTOMER/SUPPLIER/BOTH, optional plain cross-references to FleetOwner/ProcurementVendor/CrmContact ids). New `AccountingInvoiceLine` (description/quantity/unitPrice/cached lineTotal); `AccountingInvoice` gains `contactId` and `amountCredited`. New `AccountingBill`+`AccountingBillLine`+`AccountingPayablePayment` (mirrors the existing Invoice/Line/ReceivablePayment shape, reversed for payables). New `AccountingCreditNote`+`AccountingCreditNoteLine`. Migration `20260831170000_accounting_contacts_bills_credit_notes` includes a backfill that creates one `AccountingInvoiceLine` per pre-existing invoice from its own taxableAmount/description, so the new "header total = sum of lines" invariant holds for every invoice, not only new ones.
- **Multi-line invoices**: `createInvoice()`'s `taxableAmount` is now always the exact sum of its lines' `lineTotal`, computed by a new shared `computeLineItems()` reused identically by invoices, bills, and credit notes. A new shared `LineItemsEditor` client component (`src/components/forms/line-items-editor.tsx`) gives all three document types the same dynamic add/remove line-item UI, submitting as indexed `lines[{n}][...]` form fields parsed by a new `parseIndexedFormRows()` helper (`src/lib/validation.ts`).
- **Bills (payables)**: `/app/accounting/bills`, gated on `accounting.bills.manage` (create/approve/void) and `accounting.payables.manage` (record payment) - two new permissions, mirroring the existing invoices/receivables permission split. Lifecycle: `createBill()` (DRAFT) -> `approveBill()` (posts Debit expense account + input tax / Credit Accounts Payable) -> `recordBillPayment()` (the same `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` row-locked pattern `recordInvoicePayment` uses, reversed) -> PARTIALLY_PAID or PAID; `voidBill()` blocks once any payment exists and reverses the approval posting if one was made.
- **Credit notes**: `/app/accounting/credit-notes`, gated on `accounting.receivables.manage` (reusing the existing receivables permission rather than adding a new one). Settled exactly one way from DRAFT, not staged: `applyCreditNoteToInvoice()` reduces one invoice's outstanding balance (increments the invoice's new `amountCredited` column) or `refundCreditNote()` pays real cash from a chosen account. A credit note larger than an invoice's outstanding balance is rejected. `AccountingInvoice`'s outstanding-balance math (`recordInvoicePayment`'s guard and PAID-transition check, `getReceivablesSummary()`) now subtracts `amountCredited` alongside `amountPaid` everywhere.
- **New permissions**: `accounting.contacts.manage`, `accounting.bills.manage`, `accounting.payables.manage` - added to the "Accounting Manager" system role and to `ALL_PERMISSIONS` (so Organization Owner/Admin already have them, per Track 2's convention).

A new pure function `computeFleetOwnerSettlement()` does the actual math (revenue share of verified collections, minus management fee, minus verified expenses) and is fed by both `getFleetOwnerWorkspace()` (owner self-service, scoped by portal-login userId) and `listFleetOwnersWithPortfolio()` (manager-facing Owners roster, scoped by ownerId directly), so the two views can never disagree. - **Scope**: Track 4. Closes the external-repair workflow dead end, adds cost visibility before owner approval, completion invoice/evidence attachments, a correction path for verified expenses, a structural payment-to-repair link, and centralizes 5 duplicated Accounting-posting call sites.

Migration `20260831140000_fleet_maintenance_external_repairs` - purely additive (new columns with safe defaults, new enum values, one new nullable FK), so it carries none of the drop-column risk-window class of migration; applied and pushed together in the usual way regardless.

Refuses to run for an internal mechanic (`FleetMechanicNotExternalError`), so self-service scheduling is never overridden.

## 2026-08-31: Organization Admin role, Fleet/Accounting redesign Track 2 of 14

- **Scope**: Track 2. Adds a distinct "Organization Admin" system role - full cross-module management/approval capability like Organization Owner, but without owner-only powers (billing, organization settings, backups, module requests, support inbox). No schema change - this is pure permission/seed-data work, seeded automatically by `seedPlatform()` on the next deploy (already wired into `scripts/vercel-build.mjs`, runs before `next build`).
- **New permission `ORG_MEMBERS_MANAGE`**: split off the previous catch-all `ORG_SETTINGS_MANAGE`, which gated member invite/role-change/deactivate/reactivate/remove/resend/revoke *and* billing/settings/backups/module-requests/support-inbox as one undifferentiated permission. Only `src/app/app/(overview)/administration/{page.tsx,actions.ts}` now accepts either permission; every other of the ~30 `ORG_SETTINGS_MANAGE` call sites the audit found is untouched.
- **New role**: `"Organization Admin"` in `prisma/seed-data.ts`'s `SYSTEM_ROLES`/`ROLE_PERMISSIONS` - `ALL_PERMISSIONS` minus `ORG_SETTINGS_MANAGE`. New `isOrganizationAdminRole()` helper (`src/lib/auth/permissions.ts`), name+system-role gated like every other role-classification helper - automatically immune to Driver/Mechanic-style misclassification, no redirect/nav changes needed anywhere else. `src/lib/administration-roles.ts`'s existing Organization-Owner-always-assignable special case now also covers Organization Admin, so it stays selectable in the Administration page regardless of which modules an org has enabled (the generic permission-derived module check would otherwise make a broad cross-module role silently disappear from the dropdown for any org not subscribed to every module).
- **Self-escalation gap found and closed in the same change**: splitting member-management off billing/settings would otherwise let an Organization Admin grant themselves (or anyone) the Organization Owner role through the member-role-change action, since nothing previously stopped an actor with member-management rights from assigning a *more* powerful role than their own. Fixed with two independent, server-side-re-verified guards: (1) `inviteMember`/`changeMemberRole` require the actor to already hold `ORG_SETTINGS_MANAGE` to assign the Organization Owner role itself (the Administration page also drops "Organization Owner" from the role selector for a viewer who lacks it, so the UI doesn't offer what the server will reject); (2) `deactivateMember`/`removeMember` require the same permission to deactivate or remove a member who holds the Organization Owner role, so an Admin can never lock the org's own owner out. An Organization Owner's own existing rights are completely unchanged.
- **Docs**: new `docs/ADMINISTRATION_ROLES.md` - the first dedicated doc for this codebase's role/permission model (previously undocumented as its own subsystem).
- **Important files**: `src/lib/auth/permissions.ts`, `prisma/seed-data.ts`, `src/lib/administration-roles.ts`, `src/app/app/(overview)/administration/{page.tsx,actions.ts}`, `docs/ADMINISTRATION_ROLES.md` (new), `test/organization-admin-role.test.ts` (new).
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - passed. `npm run lint` - passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` - passed: 132 files (+1 new), 1032 tests (+11 net new: role/permission definition checks, and behavioral coverage - not just source-text assertion, given this is a genuine security boundary - proving an Organization Admin cannot grant/deactivate/remove Organization Owner while an Organization Owner's own existing behavior is unchanged). `npm run build` - passed.
- **No migration required** - this track is permission/seed-data only, so it carries none of the migration-timing risk of a schema-changing track.
- **Deployed and verified in production**: deployment `dpl_7jZquP9zR7hEdRQGC7Maf8d9CQpW`. `get_runtime_errors` (last 15m) reported zero errors. `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. An unauthenticated request to `/app/administration` correctly redirected to `/login`.
- **Remaining**: Tracks 3-14 (role-workspace correctness sweep, external repairs, Fleet operational expenses/owner settlement, payment reliability, and the full Ghana Accounting redesign) are next.

## 2026-08-31: Driver-to-vehicle assignment integrity, Fleet/Accounting redesign Track 1 of 14

- **Scope**: Track 1 of a 14-track Fleet/Accounting audit-and-redesign initiative (full plan in `docs/FLEET_MODULE_IMPLEMENTATION.md`'s new section and this session's approved plan). Enforces one active vehicle per driver and one active driver per vehicle - previously unenforced at every layer: `assignedDriverId` had only a plain index, the one existence check ran before and outside the write transaction (a race), and the "Assigned driver" dropdown offered every driver in the org regardless of status or existing assignment.
- **Database**: new partial unique index `FleetVehicle_organizationId_assignedDriverId_active_key` on `("organizationId","assignedDriverId") WHERE "assignedDriverId" IS NOT NULL` (migration `20260831120000_fleet_driver_assignment_integrity`) - the real concurrency backstop. New `FleetVehicleDriverHistory` table (mirrors the existing `FleetVehicleOwnershipHistory` shape).
- **Production data verified safe before migrating**: a read-only query against production confirmed zero `(organizationId, assignedDriverId)` pairs currently repeat across vehicles (only 3 vehicles org-wide have any driver assigned at all), so the unique index applies cleanly with no pre-existing conflict to clean up.
- **Service** (`src/modules/fleet/service.ts`): new `assignDriverToVehicle()`, `listActiveDriversWithAssignments()`, `filterEligibleDrivers()`; `validateDriverEligibility()` now runs inside the write transaction (was a separate, unchecked, pre-transaction lookup) and additionally checks driver `status === "ACTIVE"` and non-conflicting assignment, which it never did before. New `FleetDriverAlreadyAssignedError`/`FleetDriverNotEligibleError`, with the P2002 race path distinguished from an unrelated `assetTag`/`plateNumber` conflict via `isDriverAssignmentConflict()` so the two error paths never get confused.
- **UI**: the vehicle create/edit "Assigned driver" selector now shows only active, currently-unassigned drivers (plus the vehicle's own current driver when editing it), computed from one query and sliced per vehicle in memory rather than one query per dialog. An empty eligible list explains why instead of showing a bare dropdown.
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260831120000_fleet_driver_assignment_integrity/`, `src/modules/fleet/service.ts`, `src/app/app/fleet/vehicles/{page.tsx,actions.ts}`, `docs/FLEET_MODULE_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `test/fleet-driver-vehicle-assignment.test.ts` (new), `test/integration/tenant-isolation/fleet.test.ts` (extended).
- **Validation**: `npx prisma format`/`generate` - passed. `npx tsc --noEmit` - passed. `npm run lint` - passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` - passed: 131 files (+1 new), 1021 tests (+13 net new: eligibility rejection for inactive/cross-org/already-assigned drivers, history preservation across reassignment, a no-op-driver-resave writing no history, and the P2002-race-vs-unrelated-conflict distinction). `npm run build` - passed.
- **Guarded disposable-database integration coverage written** for the true-concurrency scenario the request explicitly required (`test/integration/tenant-isolation/fleet.test.ts`: two simultaneous `assignDriverToVehicle` calls for the same driver against two different vehicles, asserting exactly one succeeds and the other gets `FleetDriverAlreadyAssignedError`, then confirming via a fresh read that only one vehicle actually ended up with the driver) - confirmed to load and compile correctly and to fail with the guard's own explicit `TEST_DATABASE_URL is not set` refusal (not a code error) when run without one configured; actual execution against a disposable Postgres branch remains pending in this environment, the same standing, previously-disclosed limitation as every prior phase in this repository.
- **Verified live in a browser** with a temporary scratch route (removed before shipping) confirming the eligible-driver dropdown populates correctly and the empty-state message renders when no eligible drivers exist. No authenticated Fleet-Manager test-tenant credentials exist in this environment, the same standing limitation as every prior phase.
- **Process note, no production impact**: the local shell's `npx prisma migrate deploy | tail -40 && git push` piped the migrate command through `tail` before the `&&`, so the `&&` actually gated on `tail`'s exit code (always 0), not the migration's - meaning the push proceeded even though the local migrate attempt had failed with a connection error (`P1001` against the direct Neon endpoint specifically; the pooled endpoint used at runtime was reachable throughout, confirmed by a successful read-only query against it moments earlier). No harm resulted: this project's `scripts/vercel-build.mjs` already runs `prisma migrate deploy` as the first step of every production build and fails the entire build (never reaching `next build`) if it doesn't succeed - so the push alone could never have put mismatched code and schema live. Vercel's own build environment reached the direct endpoint without issue and applied the migration cleanly (confirmed in the build log: "Applying migration `20260831120000_fleet_driver_assignment_integrity`" / "All migrations have been successfully applied."). Lesson for future migration-bearing tracks: never pipe `prisma migrate deploy`'s output through another command before the `&&` that gates `git push` on it - run it unpiped, or check `$?` explicitly, so a failed migration can never appear to have succeeded.
- **Deployed and verified in production**: deployment `dpl_HsDsDVFpbDcT6VnoMR1SGWJ8yNAS`. Build log confirms the migration applied cleanly. `get_runtime_errors` (last 15m) reported zero errors. `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. An unauthenticated request to `/app/fleet/vehicles` correctly redirected to `/login`.
- **Remaining**: Tracks 2-14 (Organization Admin role, role-workspace correctness sweep, external repairs, Fleet operational expenses/owner settlement, payment reliability, and the full Ghana Accounting redesign) are next.

## 2026-08-30: Accounting integration for verified maintenance cost, Track D Phase D5 of 15

- **Scope**: D5 - formalizes the existing "verified gates reporting" convention into a real, auditable ledger posting. Verifying a completed repair's cost (`verifyRepairCompletion`, `src/app/app/fleet/maintenance/actions.ts`) now posts a Fleet Maintenance Expense entry to Accounting once verification succeeds - triggered specifically by `VERIFIED`, never by the earlier `COMPLETED` state, so an unverified repair never hits the books.
- **New - `src/lib/accounting-integration.ts`**: `postModuleExpense`/`reverseModuleExpense`, mirroring `postModuleRevenue`/`reverseModuleRevenue`'s exact contract (no-op-safe with `{posted:false, reason:"accounting-not-enabled"}` when Accounting isn't active for the organization, every failure caught and logged rather than thrown) but posting the reverse direction - debit the module's own expense account, credit the shared Cash account. A new `MODULE_EXPENSE_ACCOUNTS` map seeds `fleet: {code:"5100", name:"Fleet Maintenance Expense"}`; `AccountingAccountType.EXPENSE` already existed in the schema, so this phase needed no migration at all.
- **Call-site placement corrected from the plan's literal wording during implementation**: the plan described this as "`verifyMaintenanceCompletion` calls `postModuleExpense`," which would have put the call inside `src/modules/fleet/service.ts`. Before writing that, I checked this codebase's actual convention by reading every existing `postModuleRevenue` call site (`src/app/app/fleet/payments/actions.ts`, `src/app/app/fleet/work-and-pay/actions.ts`) and confirmed every one of them lives in the Server Action layer, never in `service.ts` - consistent with `postSourceJournalEntry`'s own documented contract that it "is deliberately not composable inside a source module's own `db.$transaction`." Implemented accordingly: `verifyMaintenanceCompletion` now returns the verified `request` (previously returned nothing) so `verifyRepairCompletion` in `maintenance/actions.ts` can call `postModuleExpense` immediately after the transaction that verifies the repair has already committed, exactly mirroring how the Fleet payments action calls `postModuleRevenue` after its own service call.
- **Skips posting for a zero/absent cost** (e.g. warranty work) rather than posting a zero-amount journal entry - checked with `request.repairCost && !request.repairCost.isZero()` before calling `postModuleExpense`.
- **Idempotency and reversal** use the same `organizationId+sourceType+sourceId+postingPurpose` identity as every other module posting (`sourceType: "FLEET_MAINTENANCE_REPAIR"`, `sourceId: request.id`, `postingPurpose: "VERIFIED"`) - a retried post is always safe, matching the documented module-boundary contract. `reverseModuleExpense` is written and exported for symmetry (delegates to the existing `reverseModuleRevenue` reversal, which doesn't care which direction the original entry posted) but has no call site yet in this codebase - there is no existing "un-verify a completed repair" action to wire it to; kept generic and ready for one.
- **No new UI surface**: the "Verify" control on the maintenance page is unchanged - only the backend behavior behind the existing action changed. A live-browser scratch-route check was skipped for this reason (nothing new to observe in a preview); correctness is covered by the tests below instead, consistent with this session's own "skip verification when the change isn't observable in the browser preview" rule.
- **Important files**: `src/lib/accounting-integration.ts`, `src/app/app/fleet/maintenance/actions.ts`, `src/modules/fleet/service.ts` (`verifyMaintenanceCompletion` now returns `request`), `docs/FLEET_MODULE_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `test/accounting-integration.test.ts`, `test/fleet-maintenance-attachments.test.ts`.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - passed. `npm run lint` - passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` - passed: 127 files, 995 tests (+10 net new: `postModuleExpense`/`reverseModuleExpense` behavioral coverage mirroring the existing revenue-posting tests, plus source-text-assertion coverage of the Action-layer wiring and the zero-cost skip). `npm run build` - passed.
- **No migration required** - this phase adds no schema, so it carries none of D3/D4's migration-ordering risk; commit/push proceeds as a normal single unit.
- **Deployed and verified in production**: deployment `dpl_9R4H9m4bruiF9n8gESFmHkmxfGtm`. `get_runtime_errors` (last 30m) reported zero errors. `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. An unauthenticated request to `/app/fleet/maintenance` correctly redirected to `/login`.
- **Remaining**: D6 (final end-to-end regression test and docs consolidation) is next and closes out the 15-phase plan.

## 2026-08-30: Multiple maintenance photo/document attachments, Track D Phase D4 of 15

- **Scope**: D4 - the UI half of D1's `FleetMaintenanceAttachment` schema work. `createFleetMaintenanceRequest`'s single optional `photo` becomes plural `photos` (up to `MAX_FLEET_MAINTENANCE_ATTACHMENTS` = 5, 1 MB each, same MIME/signature validation as before per file); every reader (`/app/fleet/maintenance`, driver-portal, mechanic-portal, the owner's per-vehicle page) switches from the single `request.photoAsset` to the plural `request.attachments`. The old `photoAssetId`/`photoAsset` field and relation are dropped entirely (migration `20260830170000_fleet_maintenance_drop_single_photo`) now that every reader is rewritten - D1's own backfill had already copied every historical single photo into its own `FleetMaintenanceAttachment` row, so this migration is pure schema cleanup with zero further data transformation.
- **Lesson from D3 applied**: this migration was written and applied directly to production only *after* every consumer sweep, test, lint, build, and this very doc/handoff entry were already finished - commit and push followed within minutes, deliberately minimizing the gap between "drop the column" and "the code that no longer needs it goes live," the exact ordering D3's incident writeup recommended.

Fixed alongside this phase's own sweep and locked in with a regression test; production currently has zero rows in either new state, so this had no live customer impact, but is disclosed here since it was a correctness gap already shipped in D3.
- **New shared `MAX_FLEET_MAINTENANCE_ATTACHMENTS` constant** (`src/modules/fleet/service.ts`) is the single source of truth for the per-report photo cap, referenced by both the manager-facing and driver-portal report forms rather than a hand-duplicated number in each.

## 2026-08-30: Fleet maintenance progress-status enum expansion, Track D Phase D3 of 15 (isolated push)

- **Scope**: D3 - the plan's own explicitly-flagged "architecturally riskiest single phase": expanding `FleetMaintenanceProgressStatus` from 6 states to 11, and wiring the real state-machine transitions those new states unlock. Pushed alone, deliberately isolated from D1/D2/D4-D6 given the migration risk - a schema-changing phase that touches every existing consumer of the enum.
- **Schema**: `FleetMaintenanceProgressStatus` gains `AWAITING_OWNER_APPROVAL`, `ASSIGNED`, `SCHEDULED`, `ON_HOLD`, `VERIFIED`, `REJECTED` (6 new values via migration `20260830160000_fleet_maintenance_status_expansion`, additive only). `FleetMaintenanceEventType` gains `REPAIR_HELD`, `REPAIR_RESUMED`, `REPAIR_WITHDRAWN` in the same migration. `REVIEWING` is kept forever (Postgres has no `DROP VALUE`) purely as a dead historical marker; `CANCELLED` is repurposed from "was actually a decline" to a genuinely new meaning (an explicit withdrawal). A second migration, `20260830160100_fleet_maintenance_status_backfill`, relabels every historical row (`REVIEWING`->`AWAITING_OWNER_APPROVAL`, an `APPROVED`-with-`mechanicId` row from D1's own backfill -> `ASSIGNED`, a verified `COMPLETED` row -> `VERIFIED`, every historical `CANCELLED` -> `REJECTED`, confirmed by reading every progress-status write site before writing this migration) and drops the now-fully-superseded `completionVerified` boolean. Production had only 3 maintenance requests total (2 `REPORTED`, 1 `CANCELLED`, none verified or mechanic-assigned) - verified with a direct read-only query before applying, and the exact expected relabeling (`CANCELLED` -> `REJECTED`, the 2 `REPORTED` rows untouched) with a second read-only query immediately after.
- **Service-layer state machine** (`src/modules/fleet/service.ts`): `managerReviewMaintenanceRequest`'s approval-required path renamed to `AWAITING_OWNER_APPROVAL`; its decline path now writes `REJECTED` (was `CANCELLED`). `ownerDecisionMaintenanceRequest`'s decline also becomes `REJECTED`; **its approval path still only ever reaches `APPROVED`** - confirmed already-correct behavior, explicitly preserved rather than "fixed," now locked in by a regression test so a future change can't reintroduce an auto-advance-to-`IN_PROGRESS` bug. `assignMaintenanceMechanic` now also sets `progressStatus: "ASSIGNED"` (previously left it untouched). `acceptMaintenanceAssignment` (D2's stub, which only recorded a date before this phase) now really transitions `ASSIGNED` -> `SCHEDULED` and refuses to run a second time on the same assignment. `startMaintenanceRepair` now requires `SCHEDULED` instead of `APPROVED`. New `holdMaintenanceRepair`/`resumeMaintenanceRepair` (`IN_PROGRESS` <-> `ON_HOLD`) and `withdrawMaintenanceRequest` (any pre-`IN_PROGRESS` state -> `CANCELLED`, the action that gives plain `CANCELLED` its real meaning going forward). `completeMaintenanceRepair` no longer sets the dropped boolean. `verifyMaintenanceCompletion` sets `progressStatus: "VERIFIED"` instead of the boolean (accounting-posting integration is D5's own job, not touched here).
- **Mechanical sweep of every other `completionVerified`/open-maintenance consumer**, all re-pointed at the new enum values rather than left silently wrong: `owner-workspace.ts`'s `OPEN_MAINTENANCE` (C1's array, relabeled and widened to include the 3 new mid-pipeline states - `ASSIGNED`/`SCHEDULED`/`ON_HOLD` - so a request doesn't silently drop off the owner's "needs attention" card the moment it moves past `APPROVED`, matching that array's original intent even though the plan's own phrasing undersold this as "just relabeled"), its two `completionVerified` filters, `owner-reports.ts`, `driver-obligations.ts`'s open-maintenance count, `driver-portal/page.tsx`'s two open-maintenance filters, `mechanic-workspace.ts`'s assigned/history split, and `investor/vehicles/[vehicleId]/page.tsx`'s verified-badge line. `getFleetInvestorSummary`'s `maintenanceOpenCount` and `getFleetManagementReport`'s `unverifiedRepairCount` each got the enum-preserving translation of their own original (and subtly different from owner-workspace's) semantics, not a one-size-fits-all replacement.
- **New shared `src/modules/fleet/maintenance-status.ts`** (`MAINTENANCE_PROGRESS_LABELS`/`MAINTENANCE_PROGRESS_BADGE`) - one source of truth for all 11 states across the manager (`/app/fleet/maintenance`), driver (`/app/fleet/driver-portal`), and mechanic (`/app/fleet/mechanic-portal`) surfaces, replacing three separately-hand-maintained copies that would otherwise have needed identical edits three times.
- **Maintenance page UI** gains Hold/Resume/Withdraw controls (new `holdRepair`/`resumeRepair`/`withdrawRequest` Server Actions) and "Start repair" now only appears once `SCHEDULED` rather than immediately after mechanic assignment. **Mechanic portal** only shows the "Schedule repair" form while an assignment is still `ASSIGNED` (unscheduled); once `SCHEDULED`, it shows the date read-only, matching `acceptMaintenanceAssignment`'s new one-shot guard.
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260830160000_fleet_maintenance_status_expansion/`, `prisma/migrations/20260830160100_fleet_maintenance_status_backfill/`, `src/modules/fleet/service.ts`, `src/modules/fleet/maintenance-status.ts` (new), `src/modules/fleet/owner-workspace.ts`, `src/modules/fleet/owner-reports.ts`, `src/modules/fleet/driver-obligations.ts`, `src/modules/fleet/mechanic-workspace.ts`, `src/app/app/fleet/maintenance/page.tsx` + `actions.ts`, `src/app/app/fleet/driver-portal/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/fleet/mechanic-portal/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/fleet/investor/vehicles/[vehicleId]/page.tsx`, `docs/FLEET_MODULE_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `test/fleet-maintenance-state-machine.test.ts` (new), `test/fleet-mechanic-roster.test.ts`, `test/fleet-owner-workspace.test.ts`.
- **Validation**: `npx prisma validate`/`format` - passed. `npx tsc --noEmit` - passed (a clean pass here was the strongest signal the consumer sweep was complete - any leftover reference to the dropped `completionVerified` field or an invalid enum literal would have failed to compile). `npm run lint` - passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` - passed: 126 files (+1 new: `test/fleet-maintenance-state-machine.test.ts`), 974 tests (+31 net new: the full mocked lifecycle walking every transition once, the owner-approval-never-auto-advances regression lock, per-transition guard-rejection tests for every new action, migration-content spot-checks, and UI-wiring source coverage; +4 existing tests updated for the renamed/relabeled enum values). `npm run build` - passed; `/app/fleet/maintenance` compiled successfully alongside everything else.
- **Migrations applied directly to production before this commit was pushed**: `npx prisma migrate deploy` ran cleanly - both migrations applied with no errors, confirmed via `npx prisma migrate status` reporting "Database schema is up to date!" immediately after.
- **Verified live in a browser** with a temporary scratch route (removed before shipping) rendering all 11 status badges and the new Hold/Resume/Withdraw action buttons with fabricated data - confirmed every label reads correctly and badge color-coding (secondary for in-flight states, default for terminal-success states, destructive for terminal-decline states) makes sense at a glance. No authenticated Fleet-Manager/Mechanic test-tenant credentials exist in this environment, the same standing limitation as every prior phase.
- **Deploy incident, disclosed transparently**: applying the migration directly to production ahead of the push (this session's standing discipline, to catch a bad migration while it's cheap) has a real cost when the migration drops a column the *currently-live* code still queries: for the several minutes between running `prisma migrate deploy` and the new deployment (`dpl_GsMy3JtPUAUR14cadMSGaBV59rNa`) actually going live, the still-serving previous deployment (`dpl_7J5pZqAKgDRx5rdfHCy8Fo2ed1Sz`, D1/D2's code) threw `P2022` (`FleetMaintenanceRequest.completionVerified does not exist`) on every request to `/app/dashboard`, `/app/fleet/maintenance`, and `/app/fleet/driver-portal` - the three pages that read that column. `get_runtime_errors` confirmed 10 occurrences across that window (`2026-08-30T18:03:47Z`-`18:08:40Z`), all attributed to the old deployment, and zero occurrences after the new deployment's `ready` timestamp (`18:09:29Z`) confirmed by a follow-up `get_runtime_errors` call scoped to `since: "2026-08-30T18:10:00Z"`. **Lesson for D4-D6 and any future column-dropping migration**: a migration that drops or renames a column the *current* deployment still queries should be applied as close as possible to the push (ideally push first, verify the build succeeds, then apply the migration once the new code is about to go live) rather than well ahead of it - the "migrate first, then do docs/commit/push" ordering used for this phase left an avoidable multi-minute error window on three fleet pages. No data was lost or corrupted; this was purely a transient read-path error during the deploy transition, and it's fully resolved on the current deployment.
- **Remaining**: D4 (multi-attachment UI, now that D1's `FleetMaintenanceAttachment` model and backfill already exist), D5 (accounting integration for verified repair cost, triggered off the new `VERIFIED` status this phase introduced), and D6 (final regression/docs consolidation) are next. D4/D5's own migrations (if any) should push immediately after being applied, per the lesson above.

A second migration, `20260830150100_fleet_mechanic_backfill`, converts every historical `mechanicAssigned` free-text value into its own `FleetMechanic` row (case-insensitive dedup per organization, earliest-recorded casing kept as canonical), re-points every request's new `mechanicId` at the right row, backfills `FleetMaintenanceAttachment` from each request's legacy single `photoAssetId`, then drops the now-fully-superseded `mechanicAssigned` column. Production had only 3 maintenance requests total, none with a mechanic assigned or a photo, so the backfill itself was effectively a no-op - verified with a direct read-only query before applying.

## 2026-08-30: AI support reliability fix, Phase B2 of 15 - persisted failure visibility, retry, structured logging

- **Scope**: the second and final phase of Track B (AI support reliability) in the 15-phase plan (see `C:\Users\andre\.claude\plans\enumerated-prancing-glade.md`, approved). Before this phase, any failed AI attempt was completely silent - a tenant's message would just sit unanswered with no visible sign anything was ever attempted. This phase makes real failures visible without ever faking a reply, while staying silent for genuinely-expected non-events (a human is already handling it; AI isn't configured; the role lacks permission).
- **`prisma/schema.prisma` / migration `20260830140000_support_system_sender_role`**: `SupportSenderRole` gains a fifth value, `SYSTEM` (additive enum value, its own migration since a new value can't be used in the same transaction that adds it). Applied directly to production and verified before pushing this commit.
- **`src/lib/ai/support-assistant.ts`**: `getAssistantReply()` now returns `{ok:true,content} | {ok:false,reason,error}` with `reason` one of `not_configured | human_online | rate_limited | no_permission | provider_error | empty_response | other`. New `logAiSupportFailure()` logs every failure with its reason (one structured `console.error`, matching this codebase's existing bracketed-tag convention). `triggerAiReplyIfEligible()` sends a tenant-visible `SYSTEM` message only for `rate_limited`, `provider_error`, `empty_response`, and `other` - the reasons where the tenant is actually waiting on something that won't resolve on its own; `human_online` (correct, expected handoff) and `not_configured`/`no_permission` (retrying can't help) stay silent by design, exactly as before this phase. The conversation is now resolved before the rate-limit check (previously the other way around) so a rate-limited reply can still be messaged into the right conversation - a deliberate small reordering, not a rewrite.
- **`src/lib/support/service.ts`**: new `sendSystemMessage(conversationId, content)`, mirroring `sendAiMessage()` exactly (no sender account, bumps no read cursor). `getTenantUnreadCount` now includes `SYSTEM` alongside `PLATFORM`/`AI`/`ADMIN`.
- **New `retryAiReply()`** Server Action (`src/app/app/(overview)/support/actions.ts`) - the tenant-facing "Try again" button's handler. Just re-runs `triggerAiReplyIfEligible()`, the same eligibility pipeline a fresh tenant message already triggers - no separate retry logic to maintain.
- **`src/components/support/support-chat.tsx`**: `SYSTEM` messages render distinctly - centered, muted, no avatar or sender name, since it's a notice from the surface itself rather than a message from any conversation participant. A "Try again" button appears under it only when it's the newest message and only for the tenant viewer (`onRetry` prop). Wired through both tenant-facing surfaces: the dedicated `/app/support` page and the floating widget (`src/components/support/floating-support-widget.tsx` gained an `onRetry` prop, wired in `src/app/app/layout.tsx`).
- **A stale doc-comment fixed in passing**: the top-of-file comment in `support-assistant.ts` still described the AI-eligibility gate as `support.isPlatformOnline()` - a leftover from before Phase B1's fix that should have been updated then. Corrected to reference `isPlatformOnlineForConversation()`.
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260830140000_support_system_sender_role/`, `src/lib/ai/support-assistant.ts`, `src/lib/support/service.ts`, `src/app/app/(overview)/support/actions.ts`, `src/app/app/(overview)/support/page.tsx`, `src/components/support/support-chat.tsx`, `src/components/support/floating-support-widget.tsx`, `src/app/app/layout.tsx`, `docs/SUPPORT_MESSAGING.md`, `test/ai-support-assistant.test.ts`, `test/support-messaging.test.ts`.
- **A real test-infrastructure bug found and fixed while writing this phase's tests, not shipped code**: `test/ai-support-assistant.test.ts`'s mocked `getGroqClient()` memoizes its result in a module-level variable computed once from `GROQ_API_KEY`. Only the one test that explicitly deleted the env var called `vi.resetModules()` before re-importing; every test after it in file order silently inherited that test's cached `null` client instead of reading its own `beforeEach`-set key, making every subsequent "eligible" test spuriously behave as `not_configured`. Fixed by moving `vi.resetModules()` into the shared `beforeEach`, so every test gets a fresh, correctly-reflecting client - eliminating a fragile "tests must stay in this exact order" footgun in the existing suite, not just the new tests this phase added.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - passed. `npm run lint` - passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` - passed: 122 files, 910 tests (+13 net new: `getAssistantReply`'s `empty_response`/`provider_error` reasons, `sendSystemMessage`, the widened `getTenantUnreadCount` role set, `triggerAiReplyIfEligible`'s full failure-reason matrix including the explicit "human_online produces no visible message" regression lock and a "retry succeeds after a first failure" test, and source-coverage checks for the SYSTEM/retry wiring). `npm run build` - passed.
- **Verified live in a browser** with a temporary scratch route (removed before shipping): a SYSTEM failure notice rendered as a centered muted card beneath the tenant's own message, with a working "Try again" button that correctly invoked the retry handler (confirmed via console log) and showed its own loading state. No authenticated tenant test-tenant credentials exist in this environment, the same standing limitation as every prior phase.
- **Deploy incident, third occurrence**: the first deploy attempt hit the same stuck-advisory-lock symptom (P1002) as Phases A1 and B1, despite the migration having already been applied and verified directly beforehand. The operator restarted Neon compute a third time, after which a retrigger deploy (commit `2cf563b`, deployment `dpl_EvJBVaGxE66DNSn82oW33kUTsmdH`) succeeded cleanly.
- **Deployed and verified in production**: `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. `get_runtime_errors` (last 1h) reported no runtime errors at all - the cleanest verification pass of any phase so far. An unauthenticated request to `/app/support` correctly redirected to the login page.
- **This closes out Track B (AI support reliability, Phases B1-B2).** Track C (Vehicle Owner dashboard/notifications) is next. The `DIRECT_URL` pooled-endpoint misconfiguration first noted in the Phase A1 entry remains unresolved and has now caused deploy friction on **three consecutive migration-bearing phases** (A1, B1, B2) - strongly recommended before Track D's first schema-changing phase, and worth prioritizing regardless given the pattern.

## 2026-08-30: AI support reliability fix, Phase B1 of 15 - conversation-scoped presence

- **Scope**: the first of Track B (AI support reliability) in the 15-phase plan (see `C:\Users\andre\.claude\plans\enumerated-prancing-glade.md`, approved). Fixes a real, confirmed bug: `isPlatformOnline()` (the check gating whether the AI assistant replies) looked at presence across *every* active Super Admin platform-wide, so one operator idly viewing any single tenant's conversation silently suppressed AI replies for *every* organization, not just the one on screen, for up to 45 seconds after their last heartbeat. The AI model itself was independently verified healthy against Groq's own deprecations page earlier in this plan - this phase is purely the presence-scoping fix, no model change.
- **`prisma/schema.prisma` / migration `20260830120000_support_presence_active_conversation`**: `UserPresence` gains a nullable `activeConversationId` (additive column only, no FK - a stale id should just fail to match on the next lookup, not cascade or require cleanup). Applied directly to production and verified before pushing this commit, learning from Phase A1's deploy trouble.
- **`src/lib/support/service.ts`**: new `isPlatformOnlineForConversation(conversationId)` - the actual AI-eligibility gate, checking the same Super-Admin presence rows as `isPlatformOnline()` but additionally requiring `activeConversationId` to match. `isPlatformOnline()` itself is untouched and stays platform-wide - it's still used for the tenant's own vague "is the team around" indicator, which was never part of the confirmed bug. `recordHeartbeat(userId, activeConversationId?)` gains an optional second parameter; omitting it leaves any previously-recorded value in place rather than clearing it, so a tenant or admin-inbox heartbeat (neither has a concept of "the platform conversation I'm viewing") can never wipe out a Super Admin's own presence state.
- **`src/lib/ai/support-assistant.ts`**: `triggerAiReplyIfEligible` now resolves the sender's own conversation first, then calls `isPlatformOnlineForConversation(conversation.id)` instead of the platform-wide `isPlatformOnline()` - a minimal reordering, not a rewrite. The hourly rate-limit check still runs first, since it only needs the organization id.
- **`src/app/app/platform/support/actions.ts` / `page.tsx`**: `platformSupportHeartbeat` gains an optional `conversationId` parameter (validated, silently ignored if malformed rather than throwing); `page.tsx` binds it to `selected.id` (`platformSupportHeartbeat.bind(null, selected.id)`), the same binding convention already used for `onSend`/`onPoll`/`onMarkRead` on that page. An immediate heartbeat on conversation-switch (per the plan) needed no new code: `SupportChat` is already mounted with `key={selected.id}`, so switching conversations remounts it and re-runs its heartbeat effect's existing immediate first call.
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260830120000_support_presence_active_conversation/`, `src/lib/support/service.ts`, `src/lib/ai/support-assistant.ts`, `src/app/app/platform/support/actions.ts`, `src/app/app/platform/support/page.tsx`, `docs/SUPPORT_MESSAGING.md`, `test/ai-support-assistant.test.ts`, `test/support-messaging.test.ts`.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - passed. `npm run lint` - passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` - passed: 122 files, 904 tests (+8 new: `isPlatformOnlineForConversation`'s three branches, `recordHeartbeat`'s optional-param behavior in both directions, a regression lock on `isPlatformOnline()` staying platform-wide, a source-coverage check that the heartbeat binding is wired, and the direct regression test proving two organizations' AI eligibility are now independent). `npm run build` - passed.
- **Migration applied directly to production before this commit was pushed**, and verified via a direct column check - a deliberate change in sequencing after Phase A1's deploy incident, so any migration problem is caught and fixed while cheap, not discovered mid-`vercel-build`. Despite that, the deploy still hit the *same* stuck-advisory-lock symptom as Phase A1 (twice: the first build attempt, then a retrigger) - confirming this is a recurring, systemic issue with this project's `DIRECT_URL` pointing at Neon's pooled endpoint rather than a genuinely transient one-off. Each time, the operator restarted the Neon compute endpoint directly to force-close the stuck connection, after which a retrigger deploy succeeded. **This env var misconfiguration should be fixed before the next migration-bearing phase** - see the Phase A1 entry for the exact recommended change (point `DIRECT_URL` at the unpooled host already available as `DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED`).
- **Deployed and verified in production**: deployment `dpl_6bWxf5ZWNY9tLCih7QvRHnSPgXr9` (second attempt, after the second Neon restart). `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. `get_runtime_errors` (last 1h) showed only the same pre-existing "no organization membership" error already noted in the Phase A2 entry, attributed to the prior deployment, not this one. An unauthenticated request to `/app/platform/support` correctly redirected to the login page (via the `admin.rockfrostgroup.com` host).
- **Remaining**: Phase B2 (persisted AI-failure visibility, a `SYSTEM` sender role, retry) is next, followed by Track C (Vehicle Owner dashboard/notifications) and Track D (Fleet maintenance workflow/Mechanic role). Fixing the `DIRECT_URL` misconfiguration before Phase B2 (which also needs a migration, for the new `SYSTEM` enum value) would avoid repeating this same deploy friction a third time.

## 2026-08-30: Support chat privacy fix, Phase A1 of 15 - per-user conversations, legacy read-only history, new organization admin inbox

- **Scope**: the first of a new 15-phase plan (Vehicle Owner/notifications/maintenance-mechanic/support-AI fixes - see `C:\Users\andre\.claude\plans\enumerated-prancing-glade.md`, approved). Fixes a real, confirmed privacy leak: `SupportConversation` was one row per organization with no `userId` column, so any active member of a tenant organization could read every other member's conversation with the Rock Frost platform, including an administrator's.
- **`prisma/schema.prisma` / migration `20260830090000_support_per_user_conversations`**: `SupportConversation` gains a nullable `userId` and a third read cursor `adminLastReadAt`; the unique constraint moves from `organizationId` alone to `[organizationId, userId]`. Every pre-migration row keeps `userId: null` as its permanent "legacy" marker (Postgres treats multiple `NULL`s in a composite unique index as distinct, so legacy rows safely coexist with new per-user rows). `SupportSenderRole` gains a fourth value, `ADMIN`, for the new organization admin inbox below.
- **`src/lib/support/service.ts` rewritten**: every tenant-keyed function now takes `(organizationId, userId)` instead of `organizationId` alone (`getOrCreateSupportConversation`, `listSupportMessages`, `sendTenantMessage`, `markReadByTenant`, `getTenantUnreadCount`). Platform-side functions move to a `conversationId` parameter, since one organization now has many conversations (`sendPlatformMessage`, `markReadByPlatform`, `setConversationStatus`); `sendPlatformMessage` throws a new `LegacyConversationError` on a pre-migration conversation - those are frozen, read-only history, never addressable again. `isTenantOnline` simplifies from an organization-wide presence aggregate to a direct single-user lookup, now that each conversation has exactly one tenant participant.
- **New organization admin inbox** (`/app/support/inbox`, `src/app/app/(overview)/support/inbox/`): gated by `PERMISSIONS.ORG_SETTINGS_MANAGE` - the same tier already used for Organization Settings, Payments, and Backups - at both the page level and independently inside every Server Action via a `requireOrgSupportAdminTenant()` helper, mirroring the platform inbox's own "never trust the page guard alone" convention. `listOrgSupportConversations(organizationId)` and `sendAdminMessage(organizationId, conversationId, ...)` both hard-scope to the admin's own organization, so a crafted `conversationId` from a different tenant is refused (`SupportNotFoundError`), not silently accepted. This corrects an early design draft that proposed declining to build this feature at all, reasoning it would "recreate the leak" - a permission-gated, single-org-scoped inbox is architecturally identical to the already-safe platform-operator inbox, not a repeat of the bug being fixed, and the user's brief explicitly asked for exactly this.
- **`src/components/support/support-chat.tsx`**: `viewerRole` and `SupportChatMessage.senderRole` widen to include `"ADMIN"`; a new `readOnly`/`readOnlyReason` prop hides the composer and quick replies and shows an explanation banner instead, used for every legacy conversation on both the platform and admin inbox surfaces. An admin's own messages render with a distinct "Admin" badge, never mislabeled as a genuine platform reply or as the tenant participant's own words.
- **`src/lib/ai/support-assistant.ts`**: `triggerAiReplyIfEligible` now resolves the sender's own conversation via `(organizationId, userId)` and targets `sendAiMessage` at that specific `conversationId`, instead of the old organization-wide send - a mechanical follow-on of the per-user conversation split, not a new AI behavior change (that's Track B, not yet started).
- **A real gap caught by direct code tracing, not by the research pass that fed the plan**: `src/app/app/layout.tsx` calls `getTenantUnreadCount(tenant.organizationId)` to drive the floating support bubble's badge for every authenticated tenant page - this call site wasn't in the plan's explicit file list and would have silently broken (wrong argument count) had it not been caught and updated to `getTenantUnreadCount(tenant.organizationId, tenant.userId)`.

## 2026-08-29: Online Collections activation, Phase B3 of 3 (final phase) - guided multi-step activation wizard, real bank picker, old single-step form retired

- **Scope**: the third and final phase of Online Collections activation (13-phase plan overall - see `C:\Users\andre\.claude\plans\enumerated-prancing-glade.md`, approved). Replaces the old single-step settlement form with a real four-step guided wizard, and introduces this codebase's first stepper/wizard UI pattern.
- **New `src/components/ui/stepper.tsx`** - a small, presentation-only step indicator (`aria-current="step"` on exactly the current step, a checkmark for completed ones). It owns no navigation state of its own; the caller drives `currentStepId`, matching this app's existing convention of storing multi-step view state in a URL search param rather than client state. Documented in `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` next to `Progress`.
- **New `src/app/app/(overview)/organization/payments/bank-options.ts`** - `loadBankOptions()` wires the already-implemented-but-previously-dead `listPaystackBanks` into a real bank picker for the first time, replacing the old free-text "Paystack bank code" input. Degrades to an empty list (never throws) when Paystack isn't configured or the live call fails.
- **The wizard** (extends `organization/payments/page.tsx`, driven by `?step=`): (1) explains the subscription-vs-operational-collections distinction; (2) collects the bank (via the new picker) and account number, calling Phase B1's `initiateSettlementProfile()`; (3) shows the Paystack-resolved account name back for confirmation and requires accepting settlement terms + confirming the beneficiary, calling `confirmSettlementBeneficiary()`; (4) previews the seven-check readiness report and, only once it reports `READY`, unlocks an "Enable online collections" control (a real `SettingsToggleRow`, not a raw checkbox) that calls `activateOnlineCollections()`.
- **A real correctness fix caught before shipping, not after**: the readiness step's checklist must be safely viewable on an ordinary page load, but `runSettlementReadinessCheck()` (Phase B1) had a side effect - promoting `VERIFIED` to `ACTIVE` - baked into the same call used for display. Fixed by adding a `commit` option (default `true`, preserving every existing caller and test unchanged) so the wizard's page render previews with `commit: false` and only the explicit "Activate" Server Action commits for real. Recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md`. A second, closely related bug was caught and fixed during implementation, before it ever ran live: the `activateOnlineCollections` action's first draft called `redirect()` for a clean "not ready" result from *inside* the same `try` block whose `catch` handler also calls `redirect()` - since `redirect()` throws internally, that structure would have made the `catch` block misreport every clean not-ready result as a failed activation attempt. Fixed by moving the not-ready check outside the `try`/`catch` entirely; a test locks this ordering in.
- **Bank name is no longer trusted from the client**: the account-setup Server Action re-derives the bank's display name from the same live Paystack bank list the picker was built from, rather than accepting a client-submitted string - a forged `bankCode` that doesn't match a real bank is rejected outright.
- **The pre-existing convention violation found during Phase B research is now fixed**: the old settlement card's raw `<input type="checkbox">` for "enable" no longer exists anywhere - it's retired along with the entire old single-step form. `saveSettlementProfile()` and `saveSettlementAccount()` had zero remaining callers once the wizard replaced their only call site, so they were deleted outright rather than kept as deprecated dead code, per this codebase's own standing convention. Workspace Settings now shows a compact settlement summary with a link to the wizard instead of duplicating the form.
- **Important files**: `src/components/ui/stepper.tsx` (new), `src/app/app/(overview)/organization/payments/bank-options.ts` (new), `src/app/app/(overview)/organization/payments/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/(overview)/organization/payments/actions.ts`, `src/app/app/(overview)/organization/settings/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/(overview)/organization/settings/actions.ts`, `src/lib/payments/operational.ts`, `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/SHARED_PAYMENTS_AND_SETTLEMENTS.md`.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - passed. `npm run lint` - passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` - passed: 121 files, 876 tests (+12 new: 3 for `Stepper`'s accessibility contract, 9 for the wizard's server-action safety properties - bank-code validation, commit-false preview safety, the redirect-outside-try/catch ordering, and the old form's complete removal - plus 2 more locking in `runSettlementReadinessCheck`'s new `commit` option). `npm run build` - passed.
- **Integration test written but not run in this environment**: `test/integration/settlement-activation-lifecycle.test.ts` (2 tests) walks `initiateSettlementProfile → confirmSettlementBeneficiary → runSettlementReadinessCheck` end to end against a real disposable Postgres database, asserting `onlineCollectionsEnabled` never flips true before a full `READY` pass and that a `SUSPENDED` profile is never silently reactivated - the Paystack HTTP calls inside `initiateSettlementProfile` are mocked (no live `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY` or real bank-resolvable account exists in this environment), everything else runs against the real database. ## 2026-08-29: Fleet Driver redesign, Phase 4 of 5 - trend visualizations wired in, plus a second existsSince-shaped correctness fix found and fixed (no schema change)

- **Scope**: wire the due-vs-paid and Work & Pay balance-reduction-over-time trend charts into the Driver Workspace per the approved plan, reusing Phase 1's already-computed obligation data (`getFleetDriverObligations`) and the already-accessible `TrendAreaChart` component - no new data-fetching function needed.
- **Due-vs-paid history**: every `ObligationCard` in the Payments tab (one per vehicle remittance, one per Work & Pay contract) now has a collapsed-by-default "Due vs. paid history" disclosure showing a two-series trend (Due, Paid) built directly from that obligation's own `summary.periods`, plus an on-time-rate stat line (`summary.onTimeRate`) shown whenever the trailing window has at least one resolved period.
- **Balance remaining over time**: each contract's card in the Work & Pay tab now shows its own on-time-rate line and a "Balance remaining over time" chart. Since Fleet stores only the contract's current `outstandingBalance`, not a balance history, the series is reconstructed by walking backward from that current figure through each trailing period's `approvedAmount` (`buildBalanceHistory` in `driver-portal/page.tsx`), then presenting it oldest-first.
- **A second correctness bug in the same family as Phase 3's, caught by browser-testing before shipping, not by the test suites**: `existsSince` (added in Phase 3) stops `isOverdue`/`isOnTime` from being computed for periods before an obligation existed, but it never touched `expectedAmount`, which every `ObligationPeriod` still carries as a constant regardless of whether the obligation existed on that date. Wiring the due-vs-paid chart straight off `summary.periods` therefore reproduced the exact failure shape Phase 3 had already fixed once: a same-day-assigned vehicle showed a flat "due GHS 200" line stretching back across the full 6-period trailing window, for days before it was ever assigned. Fixed by adding `existedYet: boolean` to `ObligationPeriod` (`src/modules/fleet/driver-obligations.ts`) and filtering both new charts on it before building their series; a chart is skipped entirely (not rendered with a single misleading point) when fewer than two real periods remain. - **The roster now shows operationally useful information, not just a contact list**: assigned vehicle(s), a payment-readiness badge (up to date / due / overdue / no obligation), current obligation with any overdue amount broken out, a pending-submissions count linking directly to the verification queue, Work & Pay completion %, and an open-maintenance badge. Two of the five summary stat tiles ("Overdue," "Pending verification") are themselves links, so a manager can identify who needs attention without opening a single driver profile - directly the acceptance criterion asked for.
- **Filters and search**: a `<form method="GET">` filter bar - search by name or plate, payment readiness, status, maintenance-attention - following the exact same GET-form convention already used by School's attendance roster (`src/app/app/school/attendance/page.tsx`), not a new client-side filtering mechanism invented for this page. Filtering happens server-side against the already-fetched roster (fleets at this app's scale don't need a second database round trip per filter change).
- **Responsive table**: secondary columns (current obligation, pending, Work & Pay, maintenance, login) collapse progressively below `md`/`lg`/`xl` breakpoints instead of forcing the whole table into horizontal scroll. - **A real correctness bug found by the integration test, not a hypothetical**: the first version of `getFleetDriverObligations`/`computeObligationSummary` (Phase 1) would show every prior period in its trailing window as "overdue" for a vehicle or Work & Pay contract that was assigned only moments ago, since it had no way to know the obligation didn't exist yet on those earlier days - it just saw "nothing submitted" and marked them overdue once closed. A new integration test creating a fresh driver/vehicle caught this immediately (`expected 'overdue' to be 'due'`). Fixed by adding an `existsSince` parameter (each vehicle's/contract's own `createdAt`) that excludes any period whose own end date falls before the obligation could have existed - not "unpaid," genuinely not applicable. Two new unit tests lock this in (a freshly-created obligation shows no fake overdue history; a long-lived one still evaluates its full trailing window normally). This fix applies retroactively to the Driver Workspace's own Overview/Payments tabs from Phase 2 as well, not just the new roster - a freshly-assigned driver will no longer see a false overdue balance on day one.

## 2026-08-29: Driver Workspace tab system, driver-scoped notifications, and a real production crash-loop fix (no schema change)

- **User feedback on the shipped Driver Workspace, with screenshots**: "the arrangement should be changed... very simple... implement tab system. Record a completed payment tab, maintenace tab. the notification should be driver's notification alone, thus payment made, payment approve, maintenace etc... dashboard doesnt work for the driver fix that behaviour." Four distinct pieces of work, tackled in order below.
- **Merged concurrent work before touching anything**: this worktree's `main` was two commits behind `origin/main` ("Improve fleet driver workflow and workspace") when this landed - a `git fetch` + clean fast-forward pulled in that agent's own Driver Workspace polish (the stat row, "Welcome, {name}" header, weekly-period normalization, date-guard validation) before any of the edits below, so nothing here overwrites it.
- **Confirmed and fixed a real, currently-live production crash, not a hypothetical**: `requireModuleAccess()`/`requirePlatformOperator()` (`src/lib/auth/module-access.ts`) both catch a tenant-resolution failure and redirect to `/app/dashboard?error=no-organization-access` - but `dashboard/page.tsx` called `requireCurrentTenant()` unconditionally, which throws the exact same error again on that redirect target, turning a recoverable failure into a raw 500. Reproduced live in a local dev session: `src/app/app/fleet/layout.tsx` has the identical pattern and threw the same error independently of that redirect chain, for the exact route (`/app/fleet/driver-portal`) the user was using. Fixed both: `dashboard/page.tsx` now uses `getCurrentTenant()` and renders the same "no organization access" message the root layout already shows on null; `fleet/layout.tsx` now uses `getCurrentTenant()` and redirects to `/login` on null, which both recovers cleanly from what is very likely a transient database hiccup between two independent per-request tenant lookups, and correctly signs out someone whose access was genuinely revoked. Documented the pattern and the reasoning in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` so the next `requireCurrentTenant()` call site is written correctly the first time. A wider audit of every remaining direct `requireCurrentTenant()` call site for the same gap is flagged as a separate follow-up, not part of this change.
- **Driver Workspace restructured into two tabs**, replacing one long scrolling page: the always-visible top section is now just the vehicle identity cards (plate, mileage, remittance target, Work & Pay pay-down progress bar) with no action buttons on them. A "Record a completed payment" tab holds the online pay-securely buttons, the "My revenue" trend card, the manual payment form, and payment history. A new "Maintenance" tab holds a "Report an issue" dialog (reusing the same vehicle-scoped validation and photo upload as the full Fleet Manager maintenance page, via a new `reportMaintenanceFromDriverPortal` action that redirects back to the Driver Workspace instead of the manager page) and a simple list of the driver's own reported issues with status badges - no manager-oriented columns (mechanic, owner approval, review controls) that a Driver can't act on anyway. Which tab opens by default is driven by a `tab` query param the new maintenance action sets on redirect, not a URL hash, since this codebase's `Tabs` component is state-driven and never mounts as anchorable DOM until its value is selected.
- **New in-app notifications for the driver's own activity** (`src/modules/fleet/service.ts`), previously nonexistent for these events: a driver submitting a payment now gets their own confirmation notification; a manager approving or rejecting that payment notifies the driver (added `driver: true` to `reviewFleetDriverPaymentSubmission`'s include to reach the linked `userId`); submitting a maintenance report notifies the reporter; a manager's approve/decline decision notifies the reporter with the actual next state (approved-and-awaiting-owner vs. approved vs. declined); a verified repair completion now also notifies whoever originally reported the issue, alongside the pre-existing owner notification (skipped when they're the same person, to avoid a literal duplicate). Every notification write for the payment-submission path sits outside that function's own try/catch, since a notification failure must never get miscategorized as the unrelated `FleetDuplicateSubmissionError` that catch block also handles.
- **`/app/notifications` scoped by role**: a Driver now sees only notifications addressed to them; every other role keeps seeing their own plus organization-wide broadcasts (a document-renewal reminder, for example) exactly as before. An org-wide broadcast was never something a Driver could act on.
