## 2026-08-28: Hero illustration loops continuously instead of playing once (no schema change)

- **Direct user correction to the entry immediately below**: "it should be continues like the one in resend, not one time." The illustration previously drew itself in once on page load and held there; the reference animation apparently loops.
- **Rebuilt as a seamless loop**: the `module-block-draw` keyframes (`src/app/globals.css`) now go through four stops - draw in (0-20%), hold fully drawn (20-70%), erase back out (70-90%), brief pause (90-100%) - on `animation-iteration-count: infinite`, a 3.2s cycle. Each block's existing `animation-delay` now staggers its phase within the recurring loop, not just its first appearance, so the cascading "modules assembling" wave keeps repeating every cycle rather than only on first load.
- **A real accessibility bug caught before shipping, not after**: this file's own site-wide `prefers-reduced-motion` rule forces `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important` on every animation. Applied blindly to an infinite loop whose keyframes end on the *erased* (hidden) state, that would have frozen the illustration invisible for reduced-motion users - the opposite of a reasonable static fallback, and worse than the previous one-shot version's behavior. Added an explicit override (`animation: none; stroke-dashoffset: 0;` inside the same media query) pinning it to the fully-drawn static state instead of relying on whichever keyframe percentage happens to be last. Reasoned through the cascade explicitly: the global rule's `!important` only touches `animation-duration`/`animation-iteration-count`, never `animation-name`, so the override's `animation: none` (which sets `animation-name: none`) wins uncontested regardless - confirmed by reasoning through CSS cascade semantics, since this environment has no way to emulate `prefers-reduced-motion` directly for an empirical check.
- **Component change to support one shared keyframe animating differently-sized blocks**: each element now exposes its own full stroke length as a `--dash-length` custom property (set inline, still computed exactly from each hexagon's own geometry) instead of a fixed inline `stroke-dashoffset`, since the keyframes need a per-element value to animate between across the whole loop, not just a one-time starting point.
- **Verified live in a browser, not just by reading the CSS**: confirmed via `getComputedStyle` that `animation-iteration-count` is `infinite` and `animation-duration` is `3.2s`; sampled the same element's live `stroke-dashoffset` twice, 800ms apart (119.2px, then 122.8px), confirming it's genuinely animating in real time rather than a static settled value.
- **Extended the regression test** (`test/module-blocks-illustration.test.ts`, now 6 tests) to assert the loop is infinite (not a one-shot `both` fill-mode), that elements use the shared `--dash-length` custom property, and that the reduced-motion override exists with the exact pinned fully-drawn state.
- **Important files**: `src/app/globals.css`, `src/components/marketing/module-blocks-illustration.tsx`, `test/module-blocks-illustration.test.ts`, `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` — passed. `npm run lint` — passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` — passed: 111 files, 802 tests (+2 new). `npm run build` — passed. No schema change, so no integration-test requirement.
- **Production deploy verified, including a direct check of the loop on the live page (not just health/error checks)**: commit `411b126` reached Vercel production deployment `dpl_2Y1UDNsyTEPQxWQNKyzSph3D2VVT` (`READY`, all production aliases attached including `app.rockfrostgroup.com`, `aliasError: null`). `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. `get_runtime_errors` (15m window, post-deploy) returned none. Loaded the actual production homepage in a real browser and confirmed via `getComputedStyle` that `animation-iteration-count` is `infinite`, and that the same element's `stroke-dashoffset` genuinely changed value (0px, then 39.8px 800ms later) - proving the loop is actively running on the live page, not just present in the shipped code.

## 2026-08-28: Every icon in the app now draws its own outline in on hover, replacing the generic zoom (no schema change)

- **Direct follow-up to the Mail/BarChart3 entry immediately below**: after seeing those two icons get a bespoke motion, the user asked "so technically on those specific icon you worked on not all the icons?" then, once told plainly that only those two of 160 distinct icon names had bespoke treatment, said "i want the effect to be on every icon in the system."
- **The honest scope problem, stated to the user before building anything**: hand-authoring a genuinely meaningful, shape-specific animation for every one of the 160 distinct `lucide-react` icon names this app imports (267 files) isn't a mechanical task - it's real per-icon design work, the same reasoning that limited the entry below to two icons. Rather than either refusing the request or quietly declaring 160 icons "done" with a formula dressed up as bespoke work, built a technique that gives every icon a real, shape-tracing animation without per-icon design effort: a "draw itself in" reveal.
- **How it works**: on hover, every `<path>`/`<rect>`/`<circle>`/etc. inside a `.lucide` icon retraces its own real stroke outline via a `stroke-dasharray`/`stroke-dashoffset` keyframe animation (`lucide-draw-in`), with each child staggered 40ms so multi-part icons trace in sequence. Because it's driven by each icon's own actual path geometry, the motion is inherently specific to that icon's shape - genuinely different from a blanket zoom - without writing 160 individual animations. Mail and BarChart3 keep their own richer, fully bespoke part-level motion from the entry below (excluded from this rule by class name) since their internal structure supports something even more specific than tracing the outline.
- **The one number that had to be measured, not guessed**: `stroke-dasharray`/`dashoffset` needs a shared length constant comfortably larger than every icon's longest real sub-path, or an icon with a longer path than that constant would render as a broken dashed line at rest (not just wrong on hover - wrong all the time). Extracted every icon name actually imported under `src/` (`grep -rhoP '(?<=import\s\{)[^}]+(?=\}\s*from\s*"lucide-react")' src --include="*.tsx"`, 160 distinct names across 267 files), rendered every one of them to static markup, injected the real markup into a live browser tab, and called `getTotalLength()` on every real sub-shape across all 160 icons - the longest observed was ~86.4 units (`BookPlus`). Used `100` as the shared constant, comfortably above that measured max, not a round number picked without checking.
- **A real tradeoff, disclosed rather than hidden**: sharing one constant across every icon means a short/simple path (e.g. `Plus`, used 81 times - the single most common icon in this app - or `X`, arrows) finishes its reveal very early in the animation and reads mostly as a quick flick, while a longer, more detailed icon (e.g. `BookPlus`, `Blocks`, `ShieldCheck`) traces visibly across the animation's full duration. This was a deliberate call, not an oversight: getting a perfectly proportional per-icon reveal speed would require measuring each icon's real length at render time (JavaScript, not pure CSS) - a materially bigger lift than a global stylesheet rule - and the resulting behavior (frequently-hovered controls like "Add" buttons feel snappy, not sluggish; decorative/detailed icons get the fuller flourish) is arguably the better outcome anyway, not just the cheaper one.
- **Verified live in a browser at the actual computed-style level, not just by reading the CSS**: confirmed the rest (non-hovered) state of a real icon resolves to `stroke-dashoffset: 0` (visually identical to before this change - solid, not dashed); confirmed hovering a real button (the floating "Contact Rock Frost support" icon) sets `animationName: "lucide-draw-in"`; injected a temporary two-path icon (`Bell`) and confirmed its two paths get `animation-delay: 0s` and `0.04s` respectively (the stagger); injected the single most-used icon in the app (`Plus`) and screenshotted it mid-hover to confirm it renders as a clean, complete plus sign, not a broken or dashed one. All temporary test elements removed after verification.
- **Important files**: `src/app/globals.css`, `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` (rewrote the "Icon hover motion" note to describe the draw-in reveal as the actual default, with the Mail/BarChart3 bespoke treatment now framed as the further exception it is).
- **Validation**: `npm run lint` — passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` — passed: 110 files, 795 tests (unchanged - purely visual CSS, exercised via the live browser checks above). `npm run build` — passed (after clearing `.next` again as a precaution, same stale-cache class of issue as the entry below, not this change).
- **Production deploy verified**: commit `4aa6227` reached Vercel production deployment `dpl_A32n4j1WH3svfdf1F9nyFnfr8sTB` (`READY`, all production aliases attached including `app.rockfrostgroup.com`, `aliasError: null`). `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. `get_runtime_errors` (15m window, post-deploy) returned none.

## 2026-08-28: Pharmacy prescription-led dispensing workflow simplified (no schema change)

- **Scope:** replaced the counter's duplicate manual entry flow with two explicit paths. **From prescription** selects one active prescription and automatically fills its patient, prescriber, outstanding medicine lines, dosage instructions, eligible stock and prices; in-stock lines start selected and support legitimate partial quantities. **Over the counter** lists only active medicines that do not require a prescription and accepts an optional walk-in patient. Dispensing numbers are now generated on the server from the pharmacy receipt prefix, date and a collision-resistant suffix.
- **Server guarantees preserved:** the UI reduction does not bypass tenant isolation, prescription-line and remaining-quantity validation, FEFO allocation, expired/quarantined/recalled stock exclusion, controlled-drug maker-checker approval, immutable audit/reversal behavior, Accounting posting, or pickup SMS behavior. The service now derives the patient and trusted prescription identifier from the selected prescription. Prescription requirements are evaluated per line, which prevents an unrelated OTC line in the same dispense from being treated as if it also required its own prescription line.
- **Interaction reference:** the workflow is aligned with the established prescription-linked model represented by FHIR `MedicationDispense`: select the authorizing prescription, review the supply lines, then record the dispense. The implementation is original and does not copy a vendor interface.

## 2026-08-28: Mail and metrics (BarChart3) icons get a bespoke, Resend-style part animation instead of the blanket zoom (no schema change)

- **Direct follow-up to the icon hover-animation entry immediately below**: the user pointed at resend.com and clarified what they actually wanted was "not just the zooming in and out like you've done" - specific per-icon motion, naming two concrete examples: "the email envelope icon opens and closes when its overed on" and "on metrics icons the bars grows up and shrink back down on hover."
- **Checked resend.com's public marketing site directly** (not their authenticated app - `/emails` redirects to a login page, so left that alone) to understand the interaction concept described, then built an original implementation of that same concept rather than inspecting or copying their actual source/assets.
- **Scoping decision, made and disclosed rather than assumed**: this app imports 160 distinct icon names from `lucide-react` across 267 files. Hand-tailoring a genuinely meaningful, shape-specific animation for every one of them isn't a mechanical task - it's real per-icon design work - so this entry covers exactly the two icon families the user named: `Mail` (6 real usages) and `BarChart3` / `lucide-chart-column` (18 real usages, the closest match to "metrics icons" in this codebase). Extending the same treatment to other icon families (Bell, TrendingUp, Send, etc.) is a reasonable follow-up, not something silently declared "done" here.
- **How it works, and why no component changes were needed**: rendered both icons to static markup to see lucide's actual internal path order (not guessed from the visual shape) - `Mail` is one `<path>` (the flap's diagonal fold lines) plus one `<rect>` (the envelope body); `BarChart3` is four `<path>`s (an axis-frame path, then three bar paths in DOM order). Both icons already carry their own per-icon lucide class (`lucide-mail`, `lucide-chart-column`) alongside the generic `lucide` class from the entry below, so this is two more scoped rules in `src/app/globals.css`, not a new component or a prop threaded through 24 call sites. `Mail`'s flap `<path>` gets `translateY(-2px) scale(1.05)` on hover (the rect never moves); `BarChart3`'s three bar `<path>`s each get `scaleY(1.35)` anchored to their own baseline (`transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: 50% 100%`) with a staggered 0/50/100ms delay for a wave rather than a snap, and `overflow: visible` on the icon so a grown bar's tip is never clipped by the 24-unit viewBox (the axis-frame path never moves). Both icons are explicitly excluded, by class name, from the blanket `scale(1.12)` rule below - they get their own motion instead of it, not in addition to it, matching the cleaner "the part moves, the icon stays anchored" read the reference site actually has.
- **Verified live in a browser at the exact per-`<path>` level, not just visually**: for `Mail`, found a real usage on the public `/contact` page and confirmed via `getComputedStyle` that hovering it resolves the flap path's transform to `matrix(1.05, 0, 0, 1.05, 0, -2)` while the rect stays `none` and the outer `<svg>` stays `none` (confirming the blanket-scale opt-out actually took). For `BarChart3` (no public page currently uses it), injected a temporary test button with lucide's exact real markup, confirmed all three bar paths resolve to `matrix(1, 0, 0, 1.35, 0, 0)` (pure Y-axis scale, no distortion) while the axis-frame path stays `none`, screenshotted it to confirm the bars render tall and uncut, then removed the test element.
- **Important files**: `src/app/globals.css`, `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` (extended the "Icon hover motion" note with this bespoke-animation addendum).
- **Validation**: `npm run lint` — passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` — passed: 110 files, 795 tests (unchanged, same as the entry below - no new test coverage for this purely visual CSS, exercised via the live browser check above instead). `npm run build` — passed after clearing a stale, unrelated `.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts` type error left over from a preceding `next dev` run on the same `.next` directory (a corrupted auto-generated file, not a real error - confirmed by deleting `.next` and rebuilding clean). No schema change, so no integration-test requirement.

## 2026-08-28: Every icon in the app now animates on hover (no schema change)

- **User request**: "i want the icons all over the system to animate when the mouse is hovered on it" - a global polish request, not scoped to one page or module.
- **Also this turn**: the user asked to log into a test tenant and keep me signed in for future browser verification. That's not something I can do directly - entering a password or creating an account is a hard operating boundary regardless of whose account it is, even when explicitly asked. Offered three alternatives via `AskUserQuestion`; the user chose to log in themselves and hand me the resulting session cookie value directly. Confirmed via `src/lib/auth/nextauth.ts` that the cookie is `httpOnly` (`__Secure-next-auth.session-token` in production), so it can only be read from DevTools' Storage panel by a human, never via page JavaScript - walked the user through that. Attempting to inject the shared value into the browser pane via `document.cookie` was blocked outright by Claude Code's own auto-mode safety classifier (matches the same pattern as entering a credential into a field), so this remains unresolved: verification this session, like every other UI change so far, is via type/lint/test/build plus a real (unauthenticated) browser check, not an authenticated click-through. Flagged this plainly rather than working around the block.
- **One-line, global CSS fix rather than touching every component**: confirmed directly (rendered a `lucide-react` icon to static markup and read the actual output) that every icon in this app carries a `lucide` class regardless of call site - `class="lucide lucide-<name> ..."` - merged with whatever className each call site already passes. That makes one scoped rule in `src/app/globals.css` sufficient for "every icon in the system," instead of a prop/wrapper change across dozens of components.
- **The rule**: `.lucide { transition: transform 160ms ease-out; }` plus `:is(button, a, [role="button"], summary):not(:disabled):hover .lucide:not(.animate-spin) { transform: scale(1.12); }`. Deliberately scoped to real interactive ancestors rather than "any hovered container," so a purely decorative icon (e.g. the plain, non-clickable module-icon grid on the public `/modules` overview page - confirmed by inspecting its actual DOM, no `<a>`/`<button>` wrapper) never gains a hover effect implying it's clickable when it isn't. `animate-spin` icons (loading spinners, 7 usages across 5 files) are explicitly excluded - stacking a hover `transform: scale()` on top of the spin keyframes' own `transform: rotate()` would have the two fight over the same CSS property and stall the spin animation. The existing site-wide `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block already zeroes every `transition-duration`, so this automatically complies with no extra work.
- **Verified live in a browser, not just by reading the CSS**: ran the local dev server, confirmed via `getComputedStyle` that hovering a real interactive icon (the floating "Contact Rock Frost support" button) resolves to `matrix(1.12, 0, 0, 1.12, 0, 0)` while genuinely `:hover`-matched, and reverts cleanly to `none` on mouse-out; separately confirmed the public `/modules` page's decorative module-grid icons correctly do *not* have an interactive ancestor and so correctly don't animate. This is the first UI change this session actually click-verified in a live browser rather than only reasoned about from source, since it didn't require an authenticated tenant.
- **Important files**: `src/app/globals.css`, `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` (new "Icon hover motion" note under Foundation, directing future icon-hover treatments to this one rule instead of a per-component one-off).
- **Validation**: `npm run lint` — passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` — passed: 110 files, 795 tests (unchanged - no test coverage exists for this purely visual CSS rule, and none was added, since it's fully exercised by the live browser check above rather than a meaningful unit-testable assertion). `npm run build` — passed. No schema change, so no integration-test requirement. `npx tsc --noEmit` not run separately for this entry - no TypeScript files changed.
- **Production deploy verified**: commit `b1bbe6d` reached Vercel production deployment `dpl_2oUEHmKeQ6mJwBgasKTX8i13Qpzh` (`READY`, all production aliases attached including `app.rockfrostgroup.com`, `aliasError: null`). `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. `get_runtime_errors` (15m window, post-deploy) returned none.

## 2026-08-28: Sidebar becomes a true click-to-expand accordion over every enabled module (no schema change)

- **User correction, direct and explicit**: an earlier entry today ("Sidebar: move collapse toggle to a hamburger icon at the top", reverted immediately below) misread a screenshot of a competitor ERP as a request to reposition the collapse toggle. The user's actual ask, confirmed with two fresh screenshots of Enerpize's real sidebar: every activated module listed at once with a chevron, and clicking *any* module - not only the one currently open - expands its own real sub-pages inline, one module open at a time. Their words: "revert this change and do exactly what im asking... if you cant do it just let me know, dont do anything you want." Reverted the wrong change first (see the entry directly below), then built exactly what the screenshots showed, confirmed via `AskUserQuestion` before starting given the scope (touches every business module's `layout.tsx`).
- **New `ModuleAccordionNav`** (`src/components/navigation/module-accordion-nav.tsx`, client component) renders every enabled module as a row with a chevron; clicking one expands its own page list in place (`useState<string | null>` for a single open section, no `useEffect` needed - every module lives under its own `layout.tsx`, so a real navigation between modules always remounts this component fresh, making the initial state always correct). Matches "current module" by each item's own `href`, not only the section's `routePrefix`, since HR/Payroll and Inventory/Procurement are each a single sidebar section backed by two separate route trees.
- **New `getFullModuleNavigation(tenant)`** (`src/platform/modules/full-navigation.tsx`) computes every enabled module's real, permission-filtered page list server-side by calling each module's own existing filtering function - `getFleetNavigationForTenant`, `getInstallmentNavigationForTenant`, `getPeopleAndPayrollNavigation`, `getInventoryProcurementNavigation` - so a role's real access can never drift between a module's own layout and the sidebar's preview of it.
- **Real bug found and fixed during development**: Fleet and Installment's permission-filtering logic used to live inline in their own `layout.tsx`. Moving it into a function `full-navigation.tsx` could call directly, inside the existing `navigation.tsx` files, broke the production build - `registry.ts` imports `navigation.tsx` for every module, `AppShell` (a Client Component) imports `registry.ts`, and `@/lib/auth/permissions` starts with `import "server-only"`, so a permission-checking function inside `navigation.tsx` poisons the client bundle. Fixed by moving that logic into new, separate `navigation-access.ts` files per module, imported only by that module's own `layout.tsx` and by `full-navigation.tsx` - never by `registry.ts`. This is the same pattern `src/modules/inventory-procurement/navigation.tsx` already documented for the same reason; a regression test now guards both files explicitly.
- **`AppShell`** gained a `moduleSections?: ModuleNavSection[]` prop, rendered via `ModuleAccordionNav` in both the desktop sidebar and the mobile sheet. Inside a business module, the flat navigation list is suppressed (`showFlatNavigation = !moduleKey`) since the current module is already the accordion's own expanded section; at the Overview/workspace scope, the flat workspace list still renders, with the accordion beneath it.
- **Superseded, in the same pass, an earlier same-day design** ("every other enabled module as a single collapsed link," `otherModuleNavItems`) that had been built for a *different* misreading of the original request - it never reached production and is fully replaced by the accordion above; `getEnabledModuleTiles` (`platform/modules/enabled-module-tiles.ts`) is still used, now by `full-navigation.tsx`.
- **Important files**: `src/components/navigation/module-accordion-nav.tsx` (new), `src/platform/modules/full-navigation.tsx` (new), `src/modules/fleet/navigation-access.ts` (new), `src/modules/installment/navigation-access.ts` (new), `src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx`, every business-module `layout.tsx` (`accounting`, `analytics`, `crm`, `fleet`, `hospital`, `hostel`, `hotel`, `hr`, `installment`, `inventory`, `payroll`, `pharmacy`, `pos`, `procurement`, `projects`, `school`) plus `src/app/app/(overview)/layout.tsx`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `test/sidebar-all-modules.test.ts` (rewritten for this design), `test/fleet-driver-sales-controls.test.ts` (route-access assertion moved to `navigation-access.ts`).

## 2026-08-28: HOTFIX - /app/dashboard and /app/accounting were crashing in production (RSC boundary violation, no schema change)

- **Live production crash, caught within minutes of the previous entry's deploy**: the user pasted actual server logs showing `/app/dashboard` erroring on every request - "Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components ... {data: ..., series: [...], valueFormatter: function p}". Root cause: the Dashboard and Accounting overview pages (Server Components) each built a `money = (value) => formatMoney(value, currency)` closure and passed it as a `valueFormatter` prop into `TrendAreaChart`/`BreakdownDonutChart` (Client Components, `charts.tsx`) - a plain JS function can never cross the React Server Component serialization boundary, only plain data and React elements can. This is a bug in the same commit as the entry directly below, not a separate regression - recorded as its own hotfix entry per this file's convention of one entry per landed change, since the previous entry was already pushed and deployed before this was caught.
- **Why the local validation gate didn't catch it**: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` both passed cleanly beforehand - this class of error is a *runtime* RSC-serialization check, not a compile-time type error (the prop types were technically valid function types on both sides). It only surfaces when the page actually renders a real request, which nothing in this environment could exercise beforehand (no test tenant credentials, and `next build`'s own static analysis doesn't simulate the flight-serialization step). Recording this plainly rather than implying the build should have caught it - it structurally could not have.
- **Fix**: `charts.tsx`'s two chart components now take a plain `currency?: string | null` prop (a serializable string) and call `formatMoney()` themselves, internally, since `formatMoney` (`src/lib/currency.ts`) has no server-only dependency and is safe to run in a Client Component. Both call sites now pass `currency={tenant.organization.currency}` instead of a function. Removed the now-dead `money` closure and its `formatMoney` import from the Dashboard page (still legitimately used elsewhere on the Accounting overview page, left in place there).
- **New regression test**: asserts neither page file nor `charts.tsx` contains `valueFormatter` again, and that both call sites pass a plain `currency` string - so this exact class of Server-to-Client function-prop bug can't silently reappear.
- **Important files**: `src/components/dashboard/charts.tsx`, `src/app/app/(overview)/dashboard/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/accounting/page.tsx`, `test/dashboard-and-accounting-trends.test.ts`.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` — passed. `npm run lint` — passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` — passed: 106 files, 729 tests (+1 from the new regression assertion). `npm run build` — passed. As noted above, none of these can independently prove the runtime RSC-boundary issue is gone the way a real page load can - the fix removes the only non-serializable prop being passed, which is the complete, correct fix for the exact error observed, not a partial mitigation.
- **Production deploy verified, with direct confirmation of the actual fix (not just health/build)**: commit `53f5d64` reached Vercel production deployment `dpl_AMdQvd5UgJAqZ79TFPdgSUh1j5in` (`READY`, all production aliases attached, `aliasError: null`) at 2026-08-28T01:11:51Z. `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. Pulled the actual runtime-error log (not just a clean/dirty check): all "Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components" occurrences are timestamped 00:54:32-00:56:17Z against the two prior (broken) deployments only; a second check scoped to `since: 2026-08-28T01:12:00Z` (after this fix went live) returned zero errors of any kind. This is the closest this environment can get to proving the exact reported crash is gone, short of a real tenant login.

## 2026-08-27: Dispensing form stopped losing every field on error, and got a real "medicine required" check (no schema change)

- **Direct follow-up to the entry immediately below**: after that fix shipped, the user came back with new screenshots and stronger feedback - clicking Dispense with the form still incomplete produced "Check the highlighted fields and try again." with nothing actually highlighted, and every field they'd entered (dispensing number, quantity, everything) was gone. Their framing: "this will make users frustrated... is this how every pharmacy management system works?"
- **Found the concrete bug behind the misleading message**: the Medicine field's `<Label required>` only draws a cosmetic asterisk - the underlying Select had no real HTML `required` wired to it, unlike Dispensing number and Quantity which do. So leaving Medicine unset let the form submit straight to the server, where `completeDispensing`'s zod schema correctly rejected the missing `medicineId`, but the resulting `?error=invalid` redirect gave no indication of which field failed and, being a hard redirect, remounted the whole server-rendered form from scratch - wiping every other field along with it. This was always possible, not something the previous fix introduced; it just became visible once real usage started.
- **Rebuilt the whole "Complete dispensing" form as a client component (`dispensing-form.tsx`) driven by `useActionState`**, converting `completeDispensing` from a "validate, then always redirect" action into one that returns `{ error, fieldErrors }` and only redirects on real success. A failed submission now re-renders in place - every uncontrolled input keeps exactly what the user typed - and the specific invalid field gets a red border plus its own inline message ("Select a medicine.", "Enter a quantity of at least 1.") instead of a vague banner pointing at nothing. Domain errors from `dispense()` itself (e.g. "An active prescription is required.") now surface the same way, inline, without touching any field the user already filled in correctly.
- **Answered their question honestly rather than defending the current design**: told the user this is a plain data-entry form, not the guided, cart-style checkout flow a purpose-built pharmacy POS typically has (barcode-first item entry, prescription-driven auto-fill, multi-line dispensing in one transaction) - that would be a real, separate redesign project if they want to pursue it, not something folded silently into this fix. Deliberately did not attempt that redesign here: scope stayed to "stop losing data and give real errors," which is what was reported and reproducible.
- **Important files**: `src/app/app/pharmacy/actions.ts` (`completeDispensing` signature changed to `(prevState, formData) => Promise<CompleteDispensingState>` - its only call site is the new client component, so this is not a breaking change for anything else), `src/app/app/pharmacy/dispensing/dispensing-form.tsx` (new), `src/app/app/pharmacy/dispensing/page.tsx`, `test/pharmacy-module.test.ts` (updated: the pre-existing "every domain error routes through runOrRedirect" regression test now separately asserts completeDispensing's own try/catch shape, since it no longer uses runOrRedirect; added a new test asserting the client-driven, non-redirecting failure path).
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` — passed. `npm run lint` — passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` — passed: 104 files, 721 tests. `npm run build` — passed. No schema change, so no integration-test requirement.
- **Not manually browser-tested against a real tenant**: no test tenant credentials in this environment, consistent with every other change this session - verified via the full type/lint/test/build gate instead. This one in particular would benefit from a real click-through post-deploy: submit with Medicine left blank and confirm the red border/inline message appear and the rest of the form survives; submit a real prescription-required medicine with no prescription selected and confirm the same.
- **Scope boundary, stated plainly**: this fixes the two concrete, reported failures (data loss, meaningless error message) and gives Medicine a real required check. It does not address the user's broader "make dispensing quicker" ask - a cart-style or barcode-first redesign is a legitimate, larger idea worth pursuing separately if wanted, not something to half-build inside a bug-fix pass.

## 2026-08-27: Dispensing's Medicine picker gave no warning before rejecting a prescription-required item (no schema change)

- **Live production report, with screenshots**: a real tenant ("Affordit Ventures") hit "An active prescription is required." on `/app/pharmacy/dispensing` while trying to dispense a specific medicine, with no prescriptions available to select (Prescription and Prescription line dropdowns both showed only "None (over-the-counter sale)"). Added a short note under the form pointing staff at Prescriptions when none is listed yet. Did not attempt to preserve the rest of the form's values across an error redirect - a genuinely separate, larger UX change (converting this from a plain server-rendered form to a client-tracked one) that's out of scope for this fix; flagged here for a future pass if this keeps coming up.

- **Found mid-task that this worktree had moved far ahead of my own last-known state**: while investigating, discovered `main` (and this checkout) already contained SMS Phases 2 and 3 in full, plus a system-wide currency-indication audit - all completed and deployed by a concurrent session using this same worktree, landing between this session's own Phase 2 push and this fix. ## 2026-08-27: SMS integration Phase 3 - per-module transactional notifications (schema migration)

- **Continues the 5-phase plan from Phase 1** (`C:\Users\andre\.claude\plans\enumerated-prancing-glade.md`). This entry covers Phase 3 only: Pharmacy, Hotel, Payroll, and Hospital can each opt into sending a customer/employee/patient an SMS when something completes, each behind its own settings toggle, off by default. The Support alert and the marketing tool remain separate, not-yet-started phases.
- **Four triggers, one shared design constraint - every send happens after its transaction has already committed, never inside it.** See the new `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry for the full reasoning: a slow or failing SMS must never roll back or delay a dispense, reservation, payroll run, or block on holding a database transaction open across a network call.
  - **Pharmacy** (`PHARMACY_PICKUP_READY`): `dispense()`'s immediate-completion path and `approveControlledDispense()`'s completion path, to `PharmacyPatient.phone`.
  - **Hotel** (`HOTEL_BOOKING_CONFIRMED`): `createHotelReservation()`, to `HotelGuest.phone`. `HotelSettings` is scoped per property, not per organization, so a multi-property org can enable this per location.
  - **Payroll** (`PAYROLL_PAYSLIP_ISSUED`): `processRun()`, one SMS per payslip after the run's transaction commits, preferring `HrEmployee.mobilePhone` over `phone`.
  - **Hospital** (`HOSPITAL_APPT_REMINDER`): the only schedule-based trigger in this phase - a new daily cron (`src/app/api/cron/appointment-reminders/route.ts`, `vercel.json`, `0 8 * * *`) finds tomorrow's `SCHEDULED` appointments at a facility with the setting on and reminds the patient, deduped against the `SmsMessage` log so a second sweep never double-texts. `HospitalSettings` is scoped per facility, same reasoning as Hotel.
- **New `src/lib/sms-templates.ts`**: pure functions for all four message bodies, mirroring `src/lib/email-templates.ts`'s pattern (no HTML escaping needed - SMS has no markup).
- **Schema migration** (`prisma/migrations/20260827003901_add_sms_module_notification_settings`): one `smsNotificationsEnabled Boolean @default(false)` column added to each of `PharmacySettings`, `HotelSettings`, `PayrollSettings`, `HospitalSettings`. Generated cleanly this time via `prisma migrate diff --from-url <test-db> --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --script` (the same clean-diff technique used for Phase 2, since `prisma migrate dev` still can't reconcile the pre-existing, already-flagged production drift) - the diff came back as exactly these four `ALTER TABLE` statements with nothing extra to trim this time.
- **Settings UI**: one new toggle added to each of the four modules' existing settings pages (Pharmacy/Hotel: `<Switch>`/`ToggleField`; Hospital/Payroll: a plain checkbox, matching each page's own existing convention), threaded through each module's existing settings action and service `update`/`upsert` function.
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260827003901_add_sms_module_notification_settings/`, `src/lib/sms-templates.ts` (new), `src/modules/{pharmacy,hotel,payroll,hospital}/service.ts`, `src/app/api/cron/appointment-reminders/route.ts` (new), `vercel.json`, `src/app/app/{pharmacy,hotel,payroll,hospital}/settings/page.tsx` and their actions files, `docs/SMS_INTEGRATION.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`.
- **Validation**: `npx prisma generate`, `npx tsc --noEmit` — passed (after renaming a shadowed `run` variable in `payroll/service.ts` and adding the new required settings field to two pre-existing integration tests and one pre-existing mocked test that construct settings objects directly). `npm run lint` — passed after removing one unused test import, zero warnings. `npm run test` — passed: 104 files, 719 tests (up from 102/711, +8: `test/sms-templates.test.ts`, `test/appointment-reminders-cron.test.ts`). `npm run build` — passed, confirmed the new `/api/cron/appointment-reminders` route compiled. `npm run test:integration -- test/integration/sms` — passed, 6 files/20 tests against the real disposable `rockfrost_test` database, including four new suites (one per module) each proving: fires exactly once when the setting is on and a phone is present, never fires when the setting is off or the phone is missing, and (Hospital only) never double-texts the same appointment on a repeated cron sweep.

Worth a manual settings-toggle-on-then-trigger-the-action click-through per module once that's set.

## 2026-08-26: SMS integration Phase 2 - SMS as an additional 2FA method alongside TOTP (schema migration)

- **Continues the 5-phase plan from Phase 1 below** (`C:\Users\andre\.claude\plans\enumerated-prancing-glade.md`). This entry covers Phase 2 only: users can now enroll in SMS-based two-factor authentication as an alternative to the existing authenticator-app (TOTP) method. Per-module notifications, the Support alert, and the marketing tool remain separate, not-yet-started phases.
- **Found this session's work was happening in the wrong checkout.** After a context-compaction gap, this session's ambient working directory had drifted to the repo's top-level clone (checked out to an unrelated branch, `codex/accounting-insights`) instead of the git worktree (`.claude/worktrees/agent+claude-main-merge2`, on `main`) where Phase 1 actually lives and was pushed from. Caught it before making any edits by comparing `git worktree list`, `.env` contents, and the presence of Phase 1's files across both locations, then moved the session into the correct worktree before writing anything. Recorded here since it's a real risk in this shared, multi-worktree environment: verify `git log`/`git branch --show-current` match expectations before resuming a schema-migration task after any gap.
- **New `TwoFactorOtpChallenge` model** (`purpose: LOGIN | ENROLL_VERIFY_PHONE | DISABLE`, hashed code, 5-minute expiry, 5-attempt limit) backs a new `src/lib/auth/sms-otp.ts` (`issueSmsOtpChallenge`/`consumeSmsOtpChallenge`/`hasPendingSmsOtpChallenge`), reusing `src/lib/sms.ts` from Phase 1 with `isOtp: true`.
- **`User.twoFactorMethod` (`TOTP | SMS`) and a new, deliberately separate `User.twoFactorPhone`** — see the new `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry: reusing the existing free-text, unverified `User.phone` field for 2FA delivery would let an attacker who already has the password redirect where login codes are sent just by editing the profile phone number, defeating 2FA in exactly the scenario it exists to stop. `twoFactorPhone` is only ever set after a code sent to that specific number is verified back.
- **Login flow required a real design change, not just a new field**: TOTP codes are computed client-side and submitted in the same request as the password, but an SMS code has to be sent by the server first. Added a pre-flight `requestLoginSmsCode(email, password)` (`src/lib/auth/actions.ts`) — a "Send code by SMS" button on the login page — that re-verifies the password (wrong attempts count toward the same `failedLoginAttempts`/`lockedUntil` lockout `authorize()` already enforces) and always returns the same generic response regardless of whether the account exists or actually uses SMS 2FA, so it can never be used to probe an email address or a 2FA method. `nextauth.ts`'s `authorize()` now branches its 2FA check on `twoFactorMethod`; the TOTP path is untouched.
- **Disabling SMS 2FA needed its own send-then-confirm step** (`requestDisableSmsCode` + a `DISABLE`-purpose branch in the existing `disableTwoFactor`), for the same reason login does — the code doesn't exist until the server generates and texts it. TOTP disable is unchanged (still password + authenticator code in one submission).
- **Found and worked around a real next-auth quirk while writing `authorize()` tests, not a bug I introduced**: this installed next-auth version's `CredentialsProvider()` factory does **not** preserve the app's `authorize()` function as the returned provider's own `.authorize` property — that's hardcoded to a `() => null` stub (confirmed by reading `node_modules/next-auth/providers/credentials.js` directly, after a test that called `.authorize()` kept silently returning `null` even with a deliberately-thrown debug error inside it). The real function only survives under `.options.authorize`. Production is unaffected (NextAuth's own core reads it from there during real request handling), but any test written against this provider must call `.options.authorize`, not `.authorize` — documented in `docs/SMS_INTEGRATION.md` and in the test file itself so a future session doesn't lose time rediscovering it.
- **Schema migration** (`prisma/migrations/20260826235127_add_sms_two_factor_auth`): `TwoFactorMethod`/`TwoFactorOtpPurpose` enums, `User.twoFactorMethod`/`twoFactorPhone`/`phoneVerifiedAt`, and the `TwoFactorOtpChallenge` table. **Hit the same category of pre-existing, unrelated schema drift as Phase 1** while generating this one — this time `prisma migrate dev` refused outright ("We need to reset the public schema") rather than just bundling extra statements. Worked around it the clean way: `prisma migrate diff --from-url <test-db> --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --script` compares the live database directly against the schema file (no shadow database, no drift-reconciliation noise) and produced exactly the intended SQL with zero unrelated statements. Hand-created the migration folder with that output and applied it via `prisma migrate deploy` (applies the file as-is, no diffing), which cleanly sidesteps `migrate dev`'s shadow-database drift block. `prisma migrate status` against the test database reports clean afterward. The pre-existing drift itself remains a separate, already-flagged item (`task_c1ea26aa` from Phase 1).
- **Important files**: `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/migrations/20260826235127_add_sms_two_factor_auth/`, `src/lib/auth/sms-otp.ts` (new), `src/lib/auth/nextauth.ts`, `src/lib/auth/actions.ts`, `src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/(overview)/account/security/{page.tsx,actions.ts}`, `docs/AUTHENTICATION_AND_AUTHORIZATION.md`, `docs/SMS_INTEGRATION.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `README.md`.
- **Validation**: `npx prisma generate` (client was stale against the new schema), `npx tsc --noEmit` — passed. `npm run lint` — passed after fixing one unescaped-apostrophe error, zero warnings. `npm run test` — passed: 102 files, 711 tests (up from 98/683, +28: `test/sms-otp.test.ts`, `test/nextauth-sms-2fa.test.ts`, `test/auth-request-login-sms-code.test.ts`, `test/account-security-sms-2fa.test.ts`). `npm run build` — passed. `npm run test:integration -- test/integration/sms` — passed, 2 files/7 tests against the real disposable `rockfrost_test` database, including the new `test/integration/sms/two-factor-otp-challenge.test.ts` (issue/consume, replay rejection, 5-attempt lockout, cascade-delete on user removal) and Phase 1's existing `sms-message.test.ts` (confirming Phase 2's migration didn't disturb it).
- **Not click-tested against the real mNotify API, and not yet manually verified in a browser**: same caveat as Phase 1 — `MNOTIFY_SENDER_ID` is still blank, so a real SMS 2FA enrollment or login will complete the full request/response cycle (challenge created, hashed, expiring correctly) but the actual text will not arrive until a sender ID is registered and configured. Worth a manual click-through of enroll → receive code → confirm → log out → log back in with a code once that's set, both for TOTP-still-works regression and the new SMS path.

## 2026-08-26: SMS integration Phase 1 - core sending capability via mNotify (schema migration)

- **User handed over a new mNotify API key with no existing integration to wire it into.** Confirmed via a full search that zero SMS-sending code existed anywhere in the codebase - the only trace was an unused `SMS` value in the `NotificationChannel` enum. When asked what to use it for, the user said "all," which resolved through scoping questions into a 5-phase plan (see `C:\Users\andre\.claude\plans\enumerated-prancing-glade.md` for the full plan, approved via plan mode): core sending capability, SMS 2FA alongside TOTP, per-module transactional notifications (Pharmacy/Hospital/Hotel/Payroll), a Support-module SMS alert, and a minimal marketing bulk-send tool. **This entry covers Phase 1 only** - core sending capability, no callers wired in yet.
- **Confirmed mNotify's actual current API before writing anything**, rather than trusting an earlier non-authoritative guess: `POST https://api.mnotify.com/api/sms/quick`, API key as a query parameter (`?key=...`, not a header or body field), recipient numbers in local Ghana format (`0XXXXXXXXX`, not international), sender ID required (max 11 chars, must be pre-registered/approved with mNotify separately), and a documented `sms_type: "otp"` field that mNotify charges extra for and warns against including on anything but an actual OTP send (directly relevant to the not-yet-built Phase 2).
- **New `src/lib/sms.ts`** mirrors `src/lib/email.ts`'s exact shape (`"server-only"`, lazy client check, warn-and-degrade to `{ok:false}` when unconfigured, never throws) plus one addition: every send, successful or failed, writes a row to a new `SmsMessage` model. **Decision, recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md`**: `SmsMessage` is a dedicated audit-log model, not a reuse of the existing `Notification` model - `Notification` has no channel filter anywhere it's read, so an SMS-audit row (no `userId`, since recipients are patients/guests/employees) would show up as an org-wide in-app bell entry for every text sent. New `src/lib/phone.ts` normalizes every phone number to mNotify's expected local format before it's used, since every phone field in this app (`PharmacyPatient.phone`, `HotelGuest.phone`, etc.) is free text with zero format validation.
- **Schema migration** (`prisma/migrations/20260826224930_add_sms_message`): `SmsMessage` model + `SmsMessageStatus` enum, plus the `Organization.smsMessages` reverse relation. **Found and worked around unrelated, pre-existing schema drift while generating this migration**: `prisma migrate dev` against the disposable test database bundled in a pile of unrelated statements (constraint/index renames on Accounting/Fleet/HR/Procurement/School tables, two dropped indexes with no replacement, `DROP DEFAULT` on `updatedAt` for 3 tables) that have nothing to do with SMS. Confirmed via `prisma migrate diff --from-url <production> --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma` that this exact same drift already exists on production today, independent of this change - almost certainly an identifier-truncation/naming-scheme mismatch from an older Prisma version. **Did not bundle this into the SMS migration**: hand-trimmed the generated `migration.sql` down to only the `SmsMessage`-related statements, verified via a second `prisma migrate diff` that the disposable test database then shows zero remaining drift for the new table specifically, and flagged the pre-existing drift separately (`task_c1ea26aa`) rather than silently fixing or silently ignoring it.
- **Disposable-database workflow note for future sessions**: the Neon branch used for this session's earlier load-testing task (`loadtest`) was found to be deleted/unreachable when reused for this phase's migration testing - a fresh branch was created instead. That branch's databases were copied from its parent, which included a pre-existing `rockfrost_test` database (already fully migrated per `docs/TESTING_STRATEGY.md`'s documented convention) - so no new database needed to be created by hand this time, just caught up on 13 already-committed-but-unapplied migrations before testing this phase's new one.
- **Note on the "25+ minute hang" mentioned below in the warehouse-fix entry's own investigation**: this session independently hit the exact same symptom (a full `npm run test:integration` run producing zero output for 25+ minutes) while validating this SMS phase, on the same `ensurePlatformSeeded()` race the warehouse-fix entry below diagnoses and fixes - stopped rather than diagnosed further here since that entry already found and fixed the real cause first. This phase's own new integration test (`test/integration/sms/sms-message.test.ts`) was run in isolation, not as part of the full suite, and passed cleanly.

- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` — passed. `npm run lint` — passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` — passed: 97 files, 680 tests (up from 667, +13: `test/sms.test.ts`, `test/phone.test.ts`). `npm run test:integration` — passed for the new `test/integration/sms/sms-message.test.ts` specifically, run in isolation (3/3, against the real disposable `rockfrost_test` database: proves `SmsMessage` rows persist correctly scoped to the sending organization, stay invisible cross-tenant, and cascade-delete with their organization). `npm run build` — passed. `prisma migrate diff` against the disposable test database confirms zero remaining drift for the `SmsMessage` table after the trimmed migration.

This raced harmlessly before, but the newly-merged pricing-catalog seed (`MODULE_PRICING_SEED`/`PRICING_BUNDLE_SEED`, ~14+ additional upserts) made `seedPlatform()` run long enough for the race window to actually get hit, throwing a real unique-constraint violation that then cascaded into a `cleanupTestOrg` `TypeError` since `beforeAll` never finished assigning `orgA`/`orgB`. Confirmed pre-existing and already failing on `main`'s own latest CI run at the time — not introduced by the warehouse fix or its branch. Fixed by having concurrent callers await one shared in-flight seed promise instead of racing on a boolean (`test/integration/setup/fixtures.ts`).
- **`main` had moved substantially since this branch was created** (10+ unrelated commits: pharmacy fixes, onboarding tours with a schema migration, an editable pricing catalogue with a schema migration, an em-dash audit, a subscription-access bug fix). ## 2026-08-26: Dispensing's Prescription picker could list a prescription that would then fail (no schema change)

- **Live production report**: a dispense with a real, selected Patient ("Quynn Hansen"), Prescription, and Prescription line still failed with "An active prescription is required." - the exact error the earlier `runOrRedirect` fix made visible instead of crashing, but the underlying cause was new.
- **Root cause**: `dispense()`'s own eligibility query (`src/modules/pharmacy/service.ts`) requires a prescription's status to be `ACTIVE`/`PARTIALLY_DISPENSED` *and* not expired (`OR: [{ expiresAt: null }, { expiresAt: { gt: new Date() } }]`). The Dispensing page's dropdown filter (`src/app/app/pharmacy/dispensing/page.tsx`) only checked status, not `expiresAt` - so a prescription that stayed `ACTIVE` in the database past its own expiry date still showed up as pickable in both the Prescription and Prescription line selects. Picking one then failed at submit with a message that read like nothing had been selected, even though it clearly had been.
- **Fixed by making the picker's eligibility filter match the service layer's exactly**: `open = rx.filter((x) => ["ACTIVE", "PARTIALLY_DISPENSED"].includes(x.status) && (!x.expiresAt || x.expiresAt > new Date()))`. An expired prescription can no longer be selected for dispensing in the first place, so the mismatch can't recur for this specific pair of checks.
- **Important files**: `src/app/app/pharmacy/dispensing/page.tsx`.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` — passed. `npm run lint` — passed, zero warnings. `npm run test` — passed: 95 files, 667 tests (up from 666, +1: asserts the page filter and the service query both carry the expiry check, so they can't drift apart again). `npm run build` — passed. No schema change.
- **Production deploy verified**: commit `95626bd` reached Vercel production deployment `dpl_4gCow561GrtEiSku5tZ38ZFqJQuV` (`READY`, all production aliases attached). `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. `get_runtime_errors` (5m window, post-deploy) returned none.

## 2026-08-25: Duplicate warehouse names no longer crash with a raw 500 (no schema change)

- **Closes the gap flagged in the 2026-08-24 "Modules page tiles are clickable again" entry below**: a real production runtime error (`PrismaClientKnownRequestError` P2002 on `InventoryWarehouse(organizationId, name)`, `POST /app/inventory/warehouses`) confirmed a user hit this — `upsertWarehouse` (`src/app/app/inventory/warehouses/actions.ts`) called `createWarehouse`/`updateWarehouse` with no handling for the existing unique constraint, so a duplicate name propagated as an unhandled exception instead of a friendly message.
- **Followed this exact module's own existing convention for this exact problem**, not the simpler blanket-`catch` pattern used elsewhere (e.g. `src/app/app/hr/configuration/actions.ts`): `src/modules/inventory/service.ts`'s `createItem`/`updateItem` already catch a Prisma P2002 and rethrow a specific typed error (`ItemSkuTakenError`/`ItemBarcodeTakenError`) that the action layer catches and maps to a specific `?error=` value. `createWarehouse`/`updateWarehouse` now do the same: a new `WarehouseNameTakenError` is thrown on P2002 (checked via `error instanceof Error && "code" in error && error.code === "P2002"`, matching this file's existing style exactly), caught in `upsertWarehouse`, and redirected to `/app/inventory/warehouses?error=duplicate` — the query-param naming matches the codebase-wide `?error=duplicate` convention the user pointed at (HR Configuration's `addEmployeeType`/`addWorkLocation`/etc.), while the detection itself stays precise to the real P2002 code rather than a blanket catch, so an unrelated failure (e.g. a dropped connection) doesn't get mislabeled as "name already in use."
- **Both create and update are covered**: `updateWarehouse` can hit the same constraint when a warehouse is renamed to a name another warehouse in the org already uses, not just on creation.
- **New `ERROR_MESSAGES.duplicate`** on `src/app/app/inventory/warehouses/page.tsx`: "A warehouse with that name already exists."
- **Important files**: `src/modules/inventory/service.ts` (`WarehouseNameTakenError`, `createWarehouse`, `updateWarehouse`), `src/app/app/inventory/warehouses/actions.ts`, `src/app/app/inventory/warehouses/page.tsx`, `test/inventory-warehouse-duplicate.test.ts` (new, 3 mocked tests: create and update both convert P2002 to `WarehouseNameTakenError`, an unrelated error still propagates unchanged), `test/integration/inventory-warehouse-unique-name.test.ts` (new, 3 real-Postgres tests: same-org duplicate create rejected, same-org rename-into-duplicate rejected, cross-org same name allowed).
- **Validation**: no schema change — the unique constraint already existed at the database level; this is an application-layer fix only. `npx prisma generate` (the worktree's client was stale against the current schema before this), `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test` (96 files, 647 tests, up from 95/644), and `npm run build` all passed. `npx prisma validate` passed using CI's own placeholder `DATABASE_URL`/`DIRECT_URL` values (none configured in this environment). **`npm run test:integration` was not run** — no `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is configured in this environment, consistent with every other change this session; the new integration test file is committed and will run for real against CI's disposable Postgres container on push.
- **Not verified live in a browser**: no test tenant credentials in this environment, consistent with every other change this session. Worth a quick manual duplicate-name submission on `/app/inventory/warehouses` to see the new inline error banner render as intended.

## 2026-08-25: Prescriber management, inline walk-in registration, dispensing receipts (no schema change)

- **Live follow-up on the same Pharmacy session**: three more gaps reported while reviewing the New Medicine form. Confirmed each, then asked the user two scoping questions (`AskUserQuestion`) before building, since both touch real design tradeoffs rather than obvious bugs: (1) how a walk-in with a paper prescription from an unregistered patient/prescriber should be handled on the Prescriptions form, and (2) what "receipt" should actually produce. User chose "quick-add inline" and "browser print view" respectively.
- **Prescriber management had the exact gap Patients had before the last fix**: "Register prescriber" was create-only, with nowhere to view, edit, or reactivate an existing prescriber. Added `updatePrescriber()` (`src/modules/pharmacy/service.ts`, scoped `{ where: { id, organizationId } }`) and an `upsertPrescriber` action (`src/app/app/pharmacy/actions.ts`), and a new "Prescribers" table on the Prescriptions page with a per-row Edit dialog (name, registration number, facility, phone, an Active toggle). `listPrescribers()` now returns every prescriber (was active-only, since it doubled as the New Prescription dropdown's source) - the dropdown itself filters to active client-side, so an inactive prescriber can no longer be picked for a new prescription but still shows in the management list to be reactivated.
- **Walk-in prescriptions can now register a new patient/prescriber inline**: the Patient/Prescriber selects on "New prescription" gained a "+ New patient (walk-in)"/"+ New prescriber" option (`src/app/app/pharmacy/prescriptions/entity-picker.tsx`, a small client component) that reveals inline fields (patient number + full name + phone; full name + registration number + facility + phone) right in the same dialog. `addPrescription` creates the patient/prescriber first when that sentinel is submitted, then the prescription itself, in one form submission - front-desk staff never has to leave the dialog to register someone first.
- **Found and fixed the same uncaught-error crash class again while building this**: `createPatient`/`createPrescriber` had no handling for their `@@unique([organizationId, patientNumber])`/`@@unique([organizationId, registrationNumber])` constraints, so a duplicate number would have crashed to Next.js's generic error page exactly like the batch-expiry/prescription-required errors fixed earlier today. Added the same P2002-to-`PharmacyStockError` conversion `createMedicine` already used, and wrapped every call site in the existing `runOrRedirect()` helper.
- **Dispensing gained a printable receipt**: `getDispensingReceipt()` (a single completed dispensing with patient/lines/medicine/batch) backs a new `/app/pharmacy/dispensing/[dispensingId]/receipt` page - pharmacy name, licence/superintendent line, receipt number, date, patient, payment method, a line-item table (medicine, batch, qty, unit price, total), and subtotal/discount/total. A "Receipt" button on each completed dispensing row opens it in a new tab; the page itself has a "Print receipt" button that calls the browser's native print dialog. Made this reusable for any future print feature in any module: `AppShell` (`src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx`) now hides its sidebar and header with `print:hidden` and removes the content padding with `print:p-0`, so any page under any module's shell prints clean without per-page chrome-hiding CSS. No PDF generation and no physical printer/cash-drawer integration - explicitly out of scope per the user's own choice of "browser print view."
- **Important files**: `src/modules/pharmacy/service.ts`, `src/app/app/pharmacy/actions.ts`, `src/app/app/pharmacy/prescriptions/{page.tsx,entity-picker.tsx}`, `src/app/app/pharmacy/dispensing/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/pharmacy/dispensing/[dispensingId]/receipt/{page.tsx,print-button.tsx}`, `src/app/app/pharmacy/payment-methods.ts` (new, shared between the Dispensing form and the receipt), `src/app/app/pharmacy/status-banner.tsx`, `src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx`, `docs/UI_UX_QUALITY_AUDIT_2026-08-25.md`.

## 2026-08-25: General UX fixes — Pharmacy patient editing, ID-leak audit, uncaught service errors, cookie consent (no schema change)

- **Dense user bug report covering 12 items**, investigated with parallel read-only research agents before any edit, then fixed by pattern where the same bug class repeated across modules. Two live production crashes were reported by the user mid-fix and are covered in this same entry.
- **Pharmacy patients could not be edited, and Notes was silently dropped when left blank.** Root cause of the Notes bug: `notes: shortText.optional()` still ran a blank submitted `""` through `shortText`'s `.min(1)`, failing the *entire* form parse — `Object.fromEntries(formData)` produces `""` for an empty input, never `undefined`, so `.optional()` alone never triggers. Added `optionalShortText`/`optionalLongText`/`optionalEmail`/`optionalCoercedDate` to `src/lib/validation.ts` (`z.preprocess` blanks to `undefined` first) and applied them across every optional field in Pharmacy's Server Actions, not just Notes. Added `updatePatient()` (`src/modules/pharmacy/service.ts`, scoped `{ where: { id, organizationId } }`, same IDOR-safe pattern as CRM's `updateContact`) and replaced `addPatient` with `upsertPatient` (`src/app/app/pharmacy/actions.ts`); `src/app/app/pharmacy/patients/page.tsx` now has a real per-row Edit dialog, a Sex select, and required-field asterisks.
- **Database ID leaking into six pages' closed select triggers**, matching the exact bug the user spotted on the Prescriptions form. Base UI's `<Select>` only reads a `<SelectValue>`'s label via an `items` prop on the `<Select>` root; without it, the closed trigger falls back to printing the raw stored value once a value is selected. Audited the whole app for the pattern and added `items={...}` to every affected select: Pharmacy's prescriptions/dispensing/stock/medicines pages, and Organization's backup-scope and theme/backup-frequency selects. Modules using a plain native `<select>` (School, Hostel, Hospital) were never affected.
- **Two live production crashes reported while this fix was underway, both the same root cause**: submitting Stock "Receive batch" with an already-expired expiry date, and completing a Dispensing sale that needed a prescription, both crashed to Next.js's generic unhandled-error page instead of showing the rejection message. Every Pharmacy Server Action called its service function directly with no `try`/`catch`, so `PharmacyStockError`/`PharmacyNotFoundError`/`PharmacyPrescriptionRequiredError`/`PharmacyWorkflowError` (already safe, user-facing messages, e.g. "Batch quantity and expiry are invalid.") went uncaught. Added a shared `runOrRedirect()` helper that catches those four classes and redirects back to the form with `?error=<message>`, applied to all twelve call sites in `src/app/app/pharmacy/actions.ts` that can throw. Added `src/app/app/pharmacy/status-banner.tsx` and wired it into every Pharmacy page so the message is actually visible. A post-deploy `get_runtime_errors` check found a third occurrence of the exact same crash class ("Insufficient eligible non-expired stock.", also from `dispense()`) that the user hit on the prior deployment before this fix went live — confirms the fix's scope (all twelve throw sites, not just the two reported) was the right call, and no new errors appeared after this deployment went `READY`.
- **Dispensing form**: "OTC/optional" and "Walk-in/optional" were real, working optional-select placeholders with confusing copy, not bugs — reworded to "None (over-the-counter sale)" and "Walk-in (no patient on file)". Payment method was a free-text input with no schema constraint; converted to a select (Cash/Card/Mobile money/Insurance/Other) matching the fixed set POS already uses correctly for its own payment method field.
- **Cookie consent banner reappearing across www/app/admin**: `serializeCookieConsent()` never set a `Domain` attribute despite `docs/COMPLIANCE_AND_ASSURANCE.md` already documenting "applies site-wide" as the intent. Now sets `Domain=.rockfrostgroup.com` only when the current hostname is actually one of the three production surfaces (never localhost or a preview deployment). Also fixed a separate SSR flash: `ConsentManagedAnalytics`'s `getServerSnapshot` was hardcoded to `() => null`; `src/app/layout.tsx` now reads the consent cookie server-side and passes it down as `initialConsent`.
- **Shared-component fixes for the loading-state and required-asterisk asks**, applied once at the primitive level rather than per-page: `src/components/forms/entity-dialog.tsx`'s shared submit button now shows a spinner and disables itself while pending (`useFormStatus`); `src/components/ui/label.tsx` gained an opt-in `required` prop rendering a red asterisk. Also converted School's student Gender field and Hostel's building Gender policy field from free text to selects.
- **Confirmed correct, no change made**: POS payment method (`src/app/app/pos/sell/sale-cart.tsx`) is already a proper select matching the `PosPaymentMethod` Prisma enum exactly. POS barcode scanning works via a standard keyboard-wedge pattern (text input + Enter), compatible with any USB/Bluetooth barcode scanner. ## 2026-08-25: Full em-dash audit across the app (no schema change)

- **User reported still seeing em dashes on the live site** after the standing AGENTS.md rule ("no em dash in customer-facing copy") had supposedly been validated all session. They asked for a full audit with zero remaining anywhere.
- **Root cause of the miss, found immediately**: every em-dash check I ran earlier this session used `grep $'—'` in Git Bash, which silently matched nothing on this Windows environment (a bash ANSI-C-quoting/encoding issue, not a real "zero occurrences" result) - `grep -c $'—' docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` reported 0 while Node's own string search on the identical file found 21. Every prior "no em dashes found" statement this session was a false negative from a broken check, not a real result. Re-verified with the Grep tool (ripgrep-backed, pastes the literal character) and Node directly, both of which agree.
- **Also found a pre-existing scope gap, unrelated to the bash bug**: the only existing automated check, `test/editorial-punctuation.test.ts`, only ever scanned `src/app/(public)` and `src/components/marketing` - the public marketing site. It had no coverage at all for the authenticated tenant/platform app (every module's pages, actions, services), which is exactly where the user was seeing them.
- **Real repo-wide audit**: 223 files contained the character in total. Triaged every one: comments/JSDoc (developer documentation, not customer-facing, correctly out of scope per AGENTS.md's own wording) vs. actual customer/user-facing strings (JSX text, error messages, descriptions, labels, table-cell fallbacks). Fixed every real violation across ~95 candidate source files (via five parallel research/fix passes, each independently verifying before editing); left `docs/**/*.md`, `test/**` descriptions, and config files (`.env.example`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `vitest*.config.ts`, `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` itself) untouched, since none of those are customer-facing per the rule's own stated scope.
- **The most common real violation, and likely exactly what the user saw**: the em dash used as a literal "no value" table-cell placeholder, e.g. `{guardian.email ?? "—"}`, across many School and Hospital pages (students, exams, classes, library, timetables, attendance, academic periods, vitals). Replaced with a plain hyphen or "N/A" depending on context. Other real violations were inline JSX separators (`{a} — {b}` to `{a}: {b}` or `{a} ({b})`), and single-sentence copy joined with an em dash where AGENTS.md's own examples (period, comma, colon, parentheses) fit naturally - e.g. error messages, page descriptions, a support quick-reply template, an OpenGraph image alt tag.
- **The regression test is now comment-aware and covers the whole app**, not just the public site. `test/editorial-punctuation.test.ts` gained a second test: it strips `//` and `/* */` comments (tracking block-comment state across line boundaries) from every `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.css` file under `src/`, then asserts no em dash survives outside a comment. The original strict "zero occurrences anywhere, including comments" check stays for just the public marketing site, unchanged. The stripper is a documented heuristic (line-based, not a real parser) rather than a guarantee - its known edge case (a string literal containing a literal "//" earlier on the same physical line as a real trailing-comment em dash) was checked against the actual codebase and does not currently occur.
- **Important files**: `test/editorial-punctuation.test.ts` (rewritten), plus the ~27 files with real fixes: `src/app/app/school/{academic-periods,attendance,campuses,classes,exams,library,reports,students,timetables,transport}/page.tsx`, `src/components/school/format.ts`, `src/modules/hospital/service.ts`, `src/app/app/hospital/{encounters/[encounterId],medication-orders}/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/pos/sell/sale-cart.tsx`, `src/app/app/platform/{organizations/actions,requests/actions,requests/_components/request-card,subscriptions/page,support/page}.tsx`, `src/app/app/(overview)/{organization/settings,organization/billing/callback/flutterwave,support}/page.tsx`, `src/app/app/projects/settings/page.tsx`, `src/app/opengraph-image.tsx`, `src/lib/support/templates.ts`.

## 2026-08-25: The earlier Affordit fix didn't actually work; real root cause fixed in code

- **Live follow-up report**: after the earlier "cancel the stale subscriptions" data fix, the user tried re-toggling the module for Affordit Ventures and it still didn't work.
- **The earlier fix was incomplete, and this entry corrects the real root cause.** `getCurrentTenant()` (`src/lib/tenant/index.ts`) queries `Subscription` rows with **no status filter** to decide which modules are "subscription-controlled" (requiring an ACTIVE, in-window subscription to grant access, regardless of `OrganizationModule.enabled`). A `CANCELLED` subscription still counted as "this module has subscription history," so cancelling the two abandoned Affordit subscriptions did not return those modules to the legacy `enabled`-only path as the earlier fix assumed. It only changed the status column; the module was still permanently gated with no way to satisfy the gate.
- **Fixed the query itself**, not the data: `db.subscription.findMany({ where: { organizationId, status: { not: "CANCELLED" } }, ... })`. `PENDING_PAYMENT`, `PAST_DUE`, `DRAFT`, and `EXPIRED` still gate access as before (an unpaid, lapsed, or still-pending agreement should still block a bare `enabled` flag) - only `CANCELLED` is excluded, since a cancelled agreement is one the platform has deliberately closed out, and an operator re-enabling the module directly afterward is a real, current decision that must not be silently overridden by a defunct record.
- **No data was deleted or further modified for Affordit.** The two subscriptions cancelled in the earlier entry stay exactly as they are (`CANCELLED`, audit-logged, zero payments); the code fix alone is what makes them stop blocking. Verified directly against production data before deploying: with the new filter, Affordit's `analytics`/`projects` modules are no longer "subscription-controlled" and both already have `OrganizationModule.enabled: true`.
- **New regression test** in `test/tenant-guard.test.ts` reproduces this exact scenario (a cancelled subscription plus a directly re-enabled module) and asserts the module is now accessible, plus asserts the real query's `where` clause carries the `status: { not: "CANCELLED" }` filter.
- **Important files**: `src/lib/tenant/index.ts`, `test/tenant-guard.test.ts`.
- **Validation**: `npx tsc --noEmit` — passed. `npm run lint` — passed. `npm run test` — passed: 95 files, 657 tests (up from 656, +1). `npm run build` — passed, 218 pages. No schema change.
- **Production deploy verified**: commit `24c465e` reached Vercel production deployment `dpl_DEtprmp9AftH5BHtMmsytdbkNgfv` (`READY`, all production aliases attached). `/api/health` returned `{"ok":true,"database":"reachable"}`. `get_runtime_errors` (10m window) returned none.
- **The broader gap flagged as `task_6401f55f` remains separately relevant**: this fix prevents a *cancelled* subscription from permanently blocking a module, but a genuinely stuck *pending/unpaid* subscription (the original Affordit scenario, before it was manually cancelled) still silently blocks a module an operator just enabled, with no warning anywhere. That task is still worth picking up.
